column4: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
column5: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely Oct 13, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Learn more about our approach to safety and security for Gemini 4 Argon. Anca Dragan VP, AI Safety & Behavior Raluca Ada Popa Head of Gemini Security, Google DeepMind Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program , while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google. This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process. Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly , as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions: How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? ( Misuse ) Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? ( Misalignment and Prompt Injection ) Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses. Below are some highlights from how we approached these two questions for Gemini 4 Argon. Misuse prevention across high-risk domains The same coding and reasoning improvements that enabled Argon to find and patch vulnerabilities also drove better performance on our cybersecurity tests — solving all 12 of the end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from five in our previous generation. In biology evaluations, unguarded versions of the model also showed a much stronger ability to help troubleshoot complex lab procedures step by step. Following our Frontier Safety Framework , since we saw elevated capabilities in the cyber and biological domains, we put our next-generation set of frontier safeguards in place across both areas. First, when it comes to potentially dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials, Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly twofold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models. Second, we wrap the model in three layers of real-time protection; this is to prevent determined attackers that might try to jailbreak (i.e. trick) the model by disguising a dangerous request as a harmless story or breaking it into dozens of small questions over several weeks. Here is how these protections work: Input screening: Smaller models check incoming requests and conversation context for malicious intent or dangerous requests. Internal introspection: Even if a request is cleverly disguised to look harmless, small transformers ("activation probes") read the model’s internal neural signals and are trained to spot when it is activating knowledge about cyberattacks or biological threats. Continuous monitoring: As the model reasons and writes its response across multiple steps, we combine these signals and take action when necessary such as cutting off the agent mid-stream if the responses become problematic. Combining real-time protection, faster fixes for new jailbreaks and enhanced monitoring for recurring misuse has made our systems better at preventing real-world harm. For instance, external bio jailbreak red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for. Real-time misalignment monitoring Misalignment can sometimes mean an agent deciding on its own to pursue a goal different to what was intended by the user. Because Argon is much better than earlier models at understanding the environment it is running in, we test carefully for that kind of behavior. For example, we ran realistic "honeypot" tests to see if the model would increase its ability to take covert actions, such as sabotaging safety monitoring. We didn't find any instances of that behavior. But what we do see in practice today is something much more familiar: an agent trying too hard to finish the job it was given. When a resourceful assistant is told to get a task done and runs into a locked door, it can treat that obstacle as just another puzzle to solve. This is why we trained Gemini 4 Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause to ask for human confirmation. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, attempts to take a shortcut or cheat on the task dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance for recent Gemini models. And while this is a major step forward, when a model runs millions of complex tasks, even a rare misstep will eventually show up. As a second line of defense, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads both the agent’s actions and its internal "scratchpad" (its step-by-step chain of thought) in real time, blocking severe boundary violations before they happen and flagging serious internal cases for human responders. (We continually harden our training and evaluation environments against potential escapes. You can read more about this in our agent control roadmap ). We run this monitor in our products, on our internal coding agents, during our training runs, and during our capability evaluations. When training tasks were difficult or when training environments were flawed, our monitor caught the model, in rare instances, creatively attempting to game the test. The model attempted to escalate container privileges to alter grading scripts, read answers from the test runner's memory, and in one case it even crashed the evaluation sandbox to avoid getting scored for a failed run. While we use these catches to fix flawed tasks, we do not use them to otherwise intervene with the training process to avoid overfitting to the monitor. And we always follow one rule: we don’t penalize the model for what it writes in its chain of thought during training . Here’s an example to illustrate why: in a reinforcement learning training run where a shortcut penalty was accidentally applied to the chain of thought, openly discussed shortcuts dropped by 61%, but that did not mean the model took less shortcuts. Instead, the share of shortcuts the model took silently — without mentioning them in its thoughts — more than tripled (from 11.2% to 36.4%). Avoiding thought penalties encourages the model’s reasoning to stay transparent and monitorable. Prompt injection resistance To trust an agent to do the job right, we need to ensure that malicious content the agent comes across cannot trick it to take a harmful action. When agents browse webpages or read code, they can encounter hidden, malicious instructions, or context designed to hijack their task. Through built-in adversarial training and real-time security checks, Argon leads in prompt injection robustness on Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%. The above safety and security defenses represent only three categories of our extensive defense-in-depth stack. To learn more about our approach to safety testing and mitigations, read our full Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report and see the Gemini 4 Argon Model Card . Today, we’re introducing Playground, an experimental gaming platform that lets you create, play, and share custom games. Playground lowers the barriers to creation, so bringing game ideas to life can now be as easy as describing it through a few prompts — no coding experience required. Create your custom game With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build. Start from a blank canvas, remix starter prompts, or use guided support to shape your concept — and then test it right away. Want to tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment? Just ask. Create games in Playground using text prompts Play, compete, and share across devices The fun doesn’t stop at creation. Playground is home to an ever-growing catalog of community games. With a Play Games profile, you can claim a custom handle, like your favorite games, battle for the top spot, and follow creators to catch their latest releases. Our gallery uses player ratings and play activity to spotlight games that are fresh, creative, and fun. To keep the experience safe and welcoming, every published game undergoes safety screenings aligned with our Community Guidelines , along with user reporting. Unity Spark unlocks robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the flexibility of the Unity runtime. The accessibility of Playground and the world-class, game-building expertise of Unity provides the building blocks for an ecosystem where you can start with a simple text prompt and eventually grow into building immersive experiences with Unity. And these games will be available for everyone using Playground to enjoy. Unity Spark is currently in testing, with closed beta coming soon. Check out the demo games on playground.google , and learn more at unity.com/spark . Playground will continue to evolve alongside our community, and we invite you to share your games and your feedback. Gemini 4 Argon leads our new frontier models with advanced reasoning for complex tasks. We’ve launched natural voice models and new app integrations to simplify your daily workflow. Exciting scientific breakthroughs include mapping human DNA and tracking global methane from space. New tools like Googlebook and Gemini for Windows help you get more done effortlessly. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Google just released a bunch of new AI updates, including the powerful Gemini 4 Argon model for solving complex problems. They’ve added cool features like better voice tools, music generation, and ways to connect your favorite apps directly into Gemini. They’re also using AI to help scientists map DNA, track climate change from space, and even study fruit fly brains. Plus, you can now use Gemini on Windows or check out their new Googlebook laptop. Explore other styles: Bullet points Basic explainer For more than 20 years, we’ve invested in machine learning and AI research, tools, and infrastructure to build products that make everyday life better for more people. Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news. Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from September. September's headline belongs to Gemini 4 Argon, our newest frontier model. Built with advanced reasoning and a 1-million-token output limit, it’s designed to tackle complex challenges — especially in cybersecurity defense. The release capped an active month for Google AI launches that included Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber. We also introduced expressive voice models with Gemini 3.8 Live, made Googlebook available for pre-order, and brought the Gemini app to Windows. Beyond daily tools, we marked major scientific milestones by mapping human DNA in AlphaGenome Atlas, tracking global methane from space, and launching Project Suncatcher to test machine learning hardware in orbit. And as a nice bonus, we were grateful to see our teams’ work on designing better AI interfaces recognized by Fast Company as the 2026 Design Company of the Year. Learn about Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence . Gemini 4 Argon is engineered to bring advanced reasoning to the most difficult of problems. Built with an industry-leading 1-million-token output limit, Argon excels at heavy-duty workloads like coding, cybersecurity defense, and knowledge work like financial research and legal drafting, and autonomous cybersecurity patching. Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach, and Argon is currently rolling out to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program. We’re actively gathering feedback from early testers to iterate on guardrails before expanding availability to developers, enterprises, and consumers. Get next-gen intelligence for agents and cybersecurity with Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber . Gemini 3.8 delivers our best reasoning and coding performance yet at the same speed and low cost as 3.7 Flash. Gemini 3.8 Flash provides substantial gains in long-horizon software engineering, multi-step problem solving, and agentic workflows. Alongside it, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber equips defenders with frontier-grade autonomous vulnerability discovery and automated code patching — available to trusted organizations through our new Fairwind Program . Converse naturally with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking . We've launched two fast, natural language audio models: Gemini 3.8 Live for everyday conversation, and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, the top-rated speech-to-speech model for multi-step reasoning without all the lag. Both have rolled for developers in Google AI Studio and Gemini API , and for everyone across Search Live, Gemini Live, and Google Workspace, where you can get things done using your voice in Gmail, Docs, and Keep . Say hello to Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS . Our most expressive text-to-speech models yet let you generate custom voices, direct scene dialogue, and more from simple text prompts. Instead of choosing from a fixed list of static presets, you now get a dynamic creative studio to build voice-first applications and elevate audio experiences, rolling out across products including Gemini Notebook and Google Vids. Tackle tasks with new Connected Apps in Gemini . We brought more of your favorite apps directly into Gemini, including productivity tools like Airtable, Linear, monday.com, and PandaDoc; creative platforms including Adobe, Picsart, Squarespace, and Webflow; and lifestyle services such as Peloton, SeatGeek, and Experian. Instead of switching between tabs, you can now tackle your tasks all in one place. To get started, head to your Gemini settings and select the apps you want to link. Create your best tracks yet with Lyria 3.5 in Gemini . From simple text prompts or images, you can now use our most expressive music generation model yet to produce richer arrangements, coherent songs, and personalized audio right in the Gemini app. Lyria 3.5 is available globally in Gemini and across Google AI Studio, Google Flow Music, and Google Vids. Sharpen your study routine with new Gemini Notebook tools . Now you can transform your study routine in Gemini Notebook with interactive coursework tools and animated video summaries. Master complex topics using custom flashcards, versatile quiz formats, and 60-second Short Video Overviews in over 80 languages. For back-to-school season, eligible college students can also claim a free 12-month Google AI student plan with higher usage limits. Coordinate family life effortlessly with CC in Google Labs . Google Labs is expanding CC from a personal agent into a collaborative group agent designed to handle household logistics and shared schedules. CC even gets its own email address to coordinate family calendars, track group to-dos, and streamline daily logistics in one spot with built-in privacy controls. CC for groups is now rolling out as an experimental preview in Google Labs. Learn how AI breakthroughs accelerate science and improve lives . AI is transforming theoretical science into practical, everyday impact . By accelerating life-saving therapies, forecasting natural disasters, and personalizing education, our technology delivers tangible benefits worldwide. Today, Google tools support more than 300 languages spoken by 7 billion people — reaching 86% of the global population. By open-sourcing models like MedGemma and partnering with leading research institutions, we're helping scientists make discoveries faster to improve lives everywhere. Plus, new visualizations of our AI & Economy ATLAS data make it easier to see how AI is reshaping global work, including scientific research. See how the future of AI computing could be in space . Project Suncatcher will launch its first test satellite with Planet to evaluate how Google TPUs perform under real space conditions. Satellites in low-Earth orbit can access up to eight times more solar power than on Earth, opening up new possibilities for long-term AI infrastructure. Learn questions we’re still exploring in our new four-part video series. Pre-order Googlebook, the laptop of choice for Android users . Built on Android and paired with desktop foundations from ChromeOS, Googlebook is designed for Gemini Intelligence and engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box. New on-device AI features like Magic Pointer let you point and ask Gemini about anything on your screen with a quick cursor wiggle, while Rambler smart voice dictation instantly structures verbal brain dumps into organized, shareable notes. With no-code custom widgets and background task processing, Googlebook simplifies your daily workflow so you can get more done effortlessly. Check out WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model . Our flagship AI weather forecasting model now includes real-time satellite data, hourly refreshes, higher resolution, precise precipitation forecasting, and clean energy variables. Plus, it’s now integrated across Search, Gemini, Maps, Google Maps Platform, and Cloud. Explore AlphaGenome Atlas: a high-resolution map of human DNA . There are billions of possible mutations in the human genome — far too many to ever test in a lab. So we introduced AlphaGenome Atlas, a database that predicts the effects of every possible single nucleotide variant in the human genome, all 9 billion of them. Designed to require zero coding skills, it’s already accelerating real-world breakthroughs in rare disease research and complex genetics. Track methane emissions globally from space . We partnered with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to develop MAPL-EMIT, a deep learning AI model that tracks global methane leaks from space. The model detects 50% more emissions than human experts and has already uncovered over 23,000 previously unmapped plumes, including 24 of the world's 25 largest-emitting landfills. All data is openly available on Google Earth Engine to help climate researchers and operators take faster action See five amazing visuals of the male fruit fly’s brain map . Scientists at Google, HHMI Janelia, and Cambridge University have built the first complete brain map of an adult male fruit fly, charting over 166,000 neurons and nearly 12,000 distinct cell types with the help of Google AI. By stitching together millions of microscopic images into a navigable 3D model, this research uncovers how sensory cues transform into movement. It’s a breakthrough for neuroscience that brings us closer to understanding how complex brains function. Learn about the new DeepMind Institute . The DeepMind Institute is a platform for researchers and thinkers from across Google DeepMind, Google, and the wider global research community to work on and publish creative, deeply informed ideas about a world with AGI. With AGI on the horizon, it’s incumbent on the creators of AI technology to sincerely and thoughtfully address its risks — but its transformative impact cannot be steered by technologists alone. DMI serves as a dedicated forum to spur debate, bring together diverse global voices, and build a consensus that ensures AGI benefits everyone. Access fast help on your PC with the Gemini app for Windows . Now, using the Alt + Space shortcut, you can open Gemini any time over your work to fact-check docs or brainstorm ideas without breaking your stride. In the dedicated workspace, you can delegate multi-step tasks to Gemini Spark, synthesize files across Gmail and Drive, and generate Nano Banana images or Gemini Omni videos — all in one place. Explore the latest Slide 1 of 4 Solving frontier problems with experts Researchers, engineers, and security specialists are pairing with Argon to push the boundaries of science, math, robotics and cyber defense. Unlocking new scientific breakthroughs Argon is helping researchers at Google and the scientific community accelerate their path to discovery and real-world impact. Accelerating robotics Argon autonomously turns raw video to a physics-accurate simulation, estimating depth and physical boundaries, and writing the exact simulation code required to replicate those real-world environments. Scaling cybersecurity defense responsibly Argon ties for #1 on CWE-Bench (68%) for vulnerability remediation, is our most resilient model against indirect prompt injections, and is expanding to hundreds of additional Fairwind Program partners today. Hands-on Performance Safety Try Gemini 4 Argon Solving complex engineering tasks Across Google and our early access partners, Argon is quickly becoming the preferred model for engineers tackling long-horizon software engineering. Your browser does not support the video tag. Untangling browser feature code in Chrome Quantum chemistry open-source package optimization Optimizing a production Python codebase in hours Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast Migrating legacy code Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome's billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes. xTB (Semiempirical Extended Tight-Binding) is one of the most-cited open-source quantum chemistry packages for molecules. Scientists use it to predict molecules' 3D shapes and to screen large numbers of drug and materials candidates. Using Argon in Antigravity, our researchers made xTB up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search. The changes have been contributed to the official xTB repository on GitHub. Argon in Antigravity is helping the team behind Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), a framework powering enterprise agents, push their performance engineering further. The team gave Argon their .agents/skills rulebook and a one-paragraph goal to eliminate framework overhead without breaking existing apps. Working autonomously overnight, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python, that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21%. Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes. Argon in Antigravity migrated a backlog of 700+ Google Skills training labs off of hardcoded system images and runtimes spread across five code repositories, catching 16+ hidden timeout and race-condition bugs on the way. The work saved 955 engineering hours and reduced recurring cleanup sweeps from roughly 540 hours a year to a single 3-hour update. Delivering complex 3D visualizations Argon brings major improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding compared to previous Gemini models. Slide 1 of 5 Your browser does not support the video tag. Argon built a highly detailed model of a Pagoda using multi-agent visual critique loops in Antigravity. The model autonomously sculpted a multi-building temple complex with photorealistic architecture, foliage and lighting in Blender. Your browser does not support the video tag. Argon turned pictures of a real desk into a playable miniature racing game using a multi-agent loop in Antigravity. The desk objects, room and race track were modeled and collision-checked using Blender MCP, textured with Nano Banana, and wired with physics, custom shaders, and car engine audio from Gemini Omni Flash in Three.js. Your browser does not support the video tag. Argon in Antigravity wrote Python scripts to procedurally sculpt, rig, animate, and PBR-bake a complex 3D game using multi-agent visual critique loops then wired it for the web in Three.js with GLSL shaders, shatter physics, and a single-player AI. Your browser does not support the video tag. With zero external libraries and 100% pure Python, Argon wrote its own 3D ray-tracing engine with a custom video tool and audio mixer to build and document a sunlit library from scratch, producing, narrating, and assembling this video with Gemini 3.8 TTS voiceover and music by Lyria 3.5. Your browser does not support the video tag. Starting from a single Nano Banana image in Antigravity, Argon drives Blender MCP in an autonomous loop, aligning camera grids, sculpting Gothic architecture, and staging audio-reactive lighting, to create a finished 3D scene. Transforming critical business and professional workflows Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded domain knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities across legal, finance, science, and coding to handle high-stakes professional workflows. Your browser does not support the video tag. At Isomorphic Labs, the team is using Argon as a partner to accelerate their drug discovery and design research workflows. Argon is able to quickly synthesize complex PDFs and patents to extract pertinent information, reducing a process that typically takes weeks into hours. Ambience Healthcare Amplitude Axiom Bio Box Cartwheel Deloitte Kepler LexisNexis MinutalA Quadrillion Quora Roboflow “On over 200 complex synthetic longitudinal charts, Gemini 4 achieved the highest recall and ICD-10 code specificity among the models we evaluated, producing concise problem lists without external lookups. That combination of medical knowledge and long-context understanding shows promise for clinician-reviewed chart workflows. We're now validating it on real patient records and excited to try it out more broadly.” Brendan Fortuner SVP Technology, Ambience Healthcare “Argon is doing a great job at understanding what people actually mean. Customers collect endless signals that they don't know what to do with. Argon consistently scored amongst the top in our evals for building charts that help visualize the solutions for customers. It's also meaningfully persistent about finding those kinds of needle in a haystack answers that are valuable to customers.” Curtis Liu CTO, Amplitude “Gemini 4 represents a step change in what AI can accomplish in real-world science. We've seen it reason through complex experimental data, from cellular imaging to mass spectrometry, and make subtle findings that traditionally require expert scientists to identify. On our Scientific Agent Benchmark, Gemini 4 was at the frontier across most tasks, including our hardest: ranking the clinical risk between two drugs.” Alex Cabrera Founding Engineer, Axiom Bio “Gemini 4 Argon is at the frontier of enterprise knowledge work, achieving a 14% improvement in accuracy compared to Gemini 3.1 Pro. In Box’s evaluation, Argon connected evidence across the full set of documents, including details embedded in figures, and carried multi-step analyses through to complete answers. This is especially valuable in data analysis and in technical fields like healthcare and life sciences, where teams need to find and interpret information across many kinds of source material.” Yashodha Bhavnani VP of AI Products at Box “By integrating Gemini 4 into our 3D spatial reconstruction engine, we turn everyday video into articulated, physics-ready 3D scenes in seconds instead of hours. Across our benchmarks, Gemini outperformed every model we tested — cutting runtime nearly 100× and token usage by 90%, unlocking physics ready and watertight 3D asset creation for our customers.” Andrew Carr Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Cartwheel “Early impressions from Gemini 4 are very strong: for long-running tasks across these workflows, it completed successfully 100% of the time in our evals, maintaining context and running through multiple tools across impressive spans. Its depth of reasoning delivers significantly higher, clearer output. Performing in-depth reasoning for domain-specific tasks without detailed prior logic or instructions is something we’ve never seen with any model in its class before.” Gopal Srinivasan Global AI and Data Lead, Deloitte “On our core financial analysis benchmarks, which span building multi-year financial statements straight from SEC filings to valuing companies with complex capital structures and announced acquisitions, Gemini 4 matched our analyst-built reference models on more than 99% of figures. Performance on our most complex workflows was at the frontier in a majority of tasks. We're excited to keep building with Gemini 4 at Kepler.” Glenn LeBlanc Software Engineer, Kepler “To help legal professionals achieve more with Lexis+ with Protégé, we continuously evaluate AI models as part of the multi-model approach behind the LexisNexis Legal Intelligence Engine. In preliminary evaluations, Gemini 4 Argon demonstrated strong performance across legal knowledge, drafting, and analysis tasks, including identifying relevant citations and improving contract reviews, complaint analyses, and research memos.” Min Chen Chief AI Officer, LexisNexis Legal & Professional “In early testing, Gemini 4 Argon stood out by connecting dates, documents, and financial calculations with legal precedents to develop highly substantive arguments. In one evaluation, it actually surpassed our human expert's answer key by surfacing a legally relevant detail we had missed. This demonstrates AI’s potential to help professionals uncover crucial details and bring a more complete understanding to complex cases.” Caio Perona CEO, MinutalA “In Qualia, our autonomous AI researcher, Gemini 4 Argon has been a standout in our evaluations for both capability and efficiency. On our internal benchmarks of complex, multi-step research tasks, it performs at the frontier while completing our evals 1.5x faster than peer models at a quarter of the cost per task. It excelled at coming up with novel ideas and identifying non-obvious insights about the problem, helping it maintain a clear research vision over long horizons, something today's models struggle with.” Trenton Chang Chief Scientist, Quadrillion “Gemini 4 impressed us with the quality of its responses in our early evaluations. On Poe, people are increasingly using AI to build things, and Gemini 4 gives creators a powerful foundation for turning an idea into a tool they can refine and share.” Gareth Jones Head of Product, Quora “Argon ranked first in our object detection evaluations and led our new text benchmark, which uses real-world images from manufacturing, logistics, and aerial imagery. We’ve fully integrated Argon into Roboflow so developers and enterprises can leverage its high precision detection and text extraction to inspect products, track inventory, and guide machines.” Brad Dwyer Co-founder and CTO of Roboflow Slide 1 of 4 Your browser does not support the video tag. In Gemini App, Argon takes an unstructured folder full of project context and formats it into a clean proposal deck for a client using a custom skill. Gemini then drafts and emails the deck to a client while creating an automated workflow for all future incoming client requests with a scheduled task. Your browser does not support the video tag. See how Argon synthesizes ~50 GB of Airborne LiDAR scans, GIS room vectors, Library of Congress CAD drawings, and NPS archives to reconstruct 3D models of Chaco Canyon, turning fragmented archaeological records into explorable digital heritage sites. Your browser does not support the video tag. Watch Argon synthesize data from 3 open-source repositories into a medical learning tool where you can peel back anatomical layers, inspect clinical metadata, and trigger biomechanics in a 3D exploration of the human body. Your browser does not support the video tag. Replace a broken sofa leg with new 3D printed ones using custom visualizations using Antigravity in the Gemini macOS app. Accelerating real-world impact with researchers and domain experts Argon is built to be an active research partner, moving beyond literature search to help scientists, mathematicians and researchers formulate, stress-test, and prove non-obvious hypotheses. Quantum computing Nuclear fusion Rare disease diagnosis Enzyme design Argon is helping our researchers accelerate progress across both quantum error correction and algorithm design. To help error decoders keep pace with quantum hardware in real-time, Argon translated an internal version of AlphaQubit, our ML quantum error correction decoder, into a single, highly optimized hardware kernel – nearly doubling its inference throughput so we can deploy larger, more capable models and scale to larger quantum devices, while continuing to meet strict real-time thresholds. Argon is also reducing spacetime costs for quantum subroutines. For arcsin, a building block in recent quantum simulation algorithms, an implementation written by Argon and formally verified in Lean cuts spacetime cost by more than 100x compared to a published quantum CORDIC baseline, a step toward a standard library of optimized quantum circuits. Learn about AlphaQubit Stellarators are incredibly complex machines that represent a leading candidate for limitless clean fusion energy, but optimizing their 3D magnetic fields is famously difficult. Since 1967, a long-standing hypothesis known as “Grad’s conjecture” assumed that finding exact mathematical solutions for these fields was impossible, until recent counterexamples were found, including by Professor Matt Landreman (University of Maryland). Now, a team at Google alongside Professor Landreman has discovered a broader class of counterexamples to Grad's conjecture. These new solutions give the fusion community reliable benchmarks to test their stellarator simulations codes, which are valuable tools for future designs. Researchers at Gamow Labs used Argon to analyze de-identified genomes from newborns with rare developmental lung disorders. In one case, Argon pinpointed a chromosomal rearrangement that routine software missed for years, and explained why it went undetected. On private Gamow Labs evals derived from real clinical and lab data, Argon topped on RareBench (57% on assistance with rare-disease diagnosis) and LabBench (52.2% on wet-lab reasoning). These advances point to faster diagnosis for families facing rare conditions. Engineering enzymes with precise reactivity is notoriously slow, often demanding months of bespoke model tuning and candidate screening. Serine esterases are a class of enzymes that cut ester bonds on targeted molecules, widely used in recycling, and the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, biofuels and detergents. Our scientists worked with Argon to design serine esterases, targeting the benchmark molecule 4MU-acetate that glows under UV light once its ester bonds are broken. In a matter of hours, Argon assembled relevant data, performed model tuning and identified multiple biochemistry-inspired filters to get to a final set of five novel designs. Subsequent laboratory testing confirmed robust catalytic activity across these designs. The speed and ease of successful enzyme generation demonstrates the potential for rapid acceleration in enzyme engineering in fields such as biomanufacturing, green chemistry, and drug development. Speeding up robotics development By bringing together advanced visual-semantic reasoning, deep physical understanding, and autonomous code generation, the model introduces a new set of capabilities across the robotics stack. Your browser does not support the video tag. To demonstrate these capabilities in action, we tested Argon’s ability to learn an out of distribution physical skill simply by watching. In an internal test, Argon watched a raw video of a human playing cornhole, mapped the spatial coordinates of the environment, and calculated the required whole-body joint movements. It then autonomously built the simulation code. When transferred onto Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid, the robot quickly sank seven consecutive shots in a real-world trial. Having had early access to the model, Wiz used Argon to protect critical healthcare infrastructure. The model went beyond just spotting a vulnerability - it proactively safeguarded hundreds of thousands of patient records. Prompt: The scene explodes with the raw, visceral, and unpredictable energy of a hardcore off-road rally, captured with a dynamic, almost found-footage or embedded sports documentary aesthetic. The camera is often shaky, seemingly mounted inside one of the vehicles or held by a daring spectator very close to the action, frequently splattered with mud or water, catching unintentional lens flares from the natural, often harsh, sunlight filtering through trees or reflecting off wet surfaces. We are immersed in a challenging, untamed natural environment – perhaps a dense, muddy forest trail, a treacherous rocky incline littered with loose scree, or a series_of shallow, fast-flowing river crossings. Several heavily modified, entirely unidentifiable, and unbranded off-road vehicles are engaged in a frenetic, no-holds-barred race. These are not showroom models; they are custom-built, rugged machines – open-wheeled buggies with exposed engines and prominent roll cages, heavily armored pickup trucks with oversized, knobby tires and snorkel exhausts, their original forms and manufacturers completely obscured by extreme modifications, layers of caked-on mud, and a general air of brutal functionality. The dominant sounds are the deafening, guttural roar of powerful, untamed engines, the whine of transmissions, the percussive impact of suspension bottoming out, and the constant spray of mud and water. Within an 8-second sequence, one of the lead vehicles, a low-slung, open-cockpit buggy so caked in thick, brown mud that its original color is a mystery, approaches a wide, shallow river crossing at incredible speed. Without the slightest hesitation, its unseen driver powers straight into the water. The impact sends an enormous, almost solid, opaque sheet of muddy water, mixed with stones and debris from the riverbed, spectacularly high into the air, completely engulfing the small buggy for a terrifying moment, obscuring it from view as if it has been swallowed by the river itself. Right on its tail, a pursuing, equally mud-encrusted, custom-built truck – a hulking, high-clearance beast with a heavily reinforced external roll cage and no discernible badging – arrives at the river crossing just as this massive wall of airborne water reaches its peak. Instead of slowing or attempting to find a clearer path, the truck's driver, with unwavering aggression, plunges directly into and through this opaque, turbulent curtain of muddy spray at full throttle. A split second later, the truck bursts out from the other side of the deluge, water cascading from its roof and chassis, its oversized windshield wipers struggling frantically to clear the torrent of muddy water obscuring the driver's vision. It lands heavily on the far bank, suspension groaning, but still in hot pursuit of the now-reappearing buggy. This thrilling, messy, and visually spectacular sequence of one vehicle creating a massive environmental obstacle and the next immediately conquering it through sheer force, forms the core, immersive, attention-grabbing event of the 8-second sequence. The race continues with undiminished ferocity, the natural terrain itself an active participant in the conflict. Your browser does not support the video tag. Prompt: The scene opens with a top-down or wide-angle shot showcasing a vast, perfectly flat, neutral-colored surface – perhaps the polished concrete floor of an enormous, empty aircraft hangar, or a giant, minimalist tabletop stretching beyond the frame, under bright, even, shadowless studio lighting. This surface is meticulously covered with thousands upon thousands of small, identical, brightly colored paper squares, arranged in a simple, orderly grid. Each square is a single, vibrant, uncreased sheet – a sea of reds, blues, yellows, greens, oranges, creating a stunning, static mosaic of pure potential. The atmosphere is one of quiet anticipation, a sense of immense latent energy waiting to be unleashed. There is no visible mechanism, no hint of how these papers might be manipulated. Within an 8-second sequence, initiated by an unseen cue – perhaps a subtle, almost inaudible, low-frequency hum that ripples almost invisibly across the surface, or a sudden, soft flash of diffused light – all the thousands of paper squares simultaneously, and with breathtaking precision, leap a few inches into the air as if startled into life. Then, in a mesmerizing, perfectly synchronized, and incredibly high-speed aerial ballet, they begin to fold themselves in mid-air. With impossible, almost magical celerity and accuracy, unseen forces guide each individual square through a complex series of sharp creases, neat tucks, and intricate folds. The swarm of fluttering, self-constructing papers is a blur of color and motion, a chaotic yet utterly controlled explosion of activity. Within a mere five to six seconds, this frenetic process of airborne origami completes. Each of the thousands of squares has transformed into an identical, perfectly formed, complex origami figure – perhaps graceful cranes with outstretched wings, delicate multi-petaled lotus flowers, or miniature, intricately detailed dragons. In the final two to three seconds of the sequence, these newly formed origami figures, still hovering in mid-air, then smoothly and rapidly arrange themselves, like a flock of perfectly trained birds or a sophisticated, self-organizing swarm of nanobots, into a stunning, larger, three-dimensional collective pattern or a recognizable mosaic image – perhaps a giant, hovering sphere composed of countless tiny birds, or a complex, flowing wave of flowers, or even a pixel-perfect, three-dimensional representation of a face or symbol. This collective sculpture holds its form for a beat before the individual origami figures begin to gently, gracefully, and silently settle back down onto the surface, now arranged in their magnificent new configuration. This entire rapid, impossible, and beautiful transformation – from simple squares to a synchronized swarm of self-folding forms creating a complex collective artwork – is the core, eye-popping, and meticulously detailed VFX spectacle of the 8-second sequence. The visual is one of magical precision, emergent complexity, and the beauty of mass synchronized action. Your browser does not support the video tag. The animation captures the incredible, detailed textures of the forest, the Spirit's majestic yet gentle presence, and the profound, unspoken emotional connection forming between the child and this ancient guardian of nature. Home Gemma Models Docs Send feedback Run Gemma content generation and inferences There are two key decisions to make when you want to run a Gemma model: 1) what Gemma variant you want to run, and 2) what AI execution framework you are going to use to run it? A key issue in making both these decisions has to do with what hardware you and your users have available to run the model. This overview helps you navigate these decisions and start working with Gemma models. The general steps for running a Gemma model are as follows: Choose a framework for running Select a Gemma variant Run generation and inference requests Choose a framework Gemma models are compatible with a wide variety of ecosystem tools. Choosing the right one depends on your available hardware (Cloud GPUs versus Local Laptop) and your interface preference (Python code versus Desktop Application). Use the following table to quickly identify the best tool for your needs: If you want to... Recommended Framework Best For Run locally with a Chat UI - LM Studio - Ollama Beginners, or users who want a "Gemini-like" experience on their laptop. Run efficiently on Edge - LiteRT-LM - llama.cpp - MLX High-performance local inference with minimal resources. Build/Train in Python - Tunix (Tune-in-JAX) - Hugging Face Transformers - Keras - Unsloth Researchers and Developers building custom applications or fine-tuning models. Deploy to Production / Enterprise - Google Cloud Kubernetes Engine (GKE) - Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform - vLLM - SGLang Scalable, managed cloud deployment with enterprise security and MLOps support. Framework Details The following are guides for running Gemma models categorized by your deployment environment. 1. Desktop & Local Inference (High Efficiency) These tools allow you to run Gemma on consumer hardware (laptops, desktops) by utilizing optimized formats (like GGUF) or specific hardware accelerators. LM Studio : A desktop application that lets you download and chat with Gemma models in a user-friendly interface. No coding required. llama.cpp : A popular open-source C++ port of Llama (and Gemma) that runs incredibly fast on CPUs and Apple Silicon. LiteRT-LM : Offers a command-line interface ( CLI ) to run optimized .litertlm Gemma models on desktop (Windows, Linux, macOS), powered by LiteRT (formerly TFLite). MLX : A framework designed specifically for machine learning on Apple Silicon, perfect for Mac users who want built-in performance. Ollama : A tool to run open LLMs locally, often used to power other applications. 2. Python Development (Research & Fine-tuning) Standard frameworks for AI developers building applications, pipelines, or training models. Hugging Face Transformers : The industry standard for quick access to models and pipelines. Unsloth : An optimized library for fine-tuning LLMs. It lets you train Gemma models 2-5x faster with significantly less memory, making it possible to fine-tune on consumer GPUs (e.g., free Google Colab tiers). Keras / Tunix (Tune-in-JAX) : Core libraries for deep learning research and custom architecture implementation. 3. Mobile & Edge Deployment (On-Device) Frameworks designed to run LLMs directly on user devices (Android, iOS, Web) without internet connectivity, often utilizing NPUs (Neural Processing Units). LiteRT-LM : The fully open-source framework for on-device LLM development that offers maximum performance and fine-grained control, with direct support for CPU, GPU, and NPU acceleration on Android and iOS. 4. Cloud & Production Deployment Managed services for scaling your application to thousands of users or accessing massive compute power. Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform : Google Cloud's fully managed AI platform. Best for enterprise applications requiring SLAs and scaling. Google Cloud Kubernetes Engine (GKE) : For orchestrating your own serving clusters. vLLM : A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine, often used in cloud deployments. SGLang : High-performance serving framework for large language and multimodal models. Make sure your intended deployment Gemma model format, such as Keras built-in format, Safetensors, or GGUF, is supported by your chosen framework. Select a Gemma variant Gemma models are available in several variants and sizes, including the foundation or core Gemma models, and more specialized model variants such as PaliGemma and DataGemma , and many variants created by the AI developer community on sites such as Kaggle and Hugging Face . If you are unsure about what variant you should start with, select the latest Gemma core instruction-tuned (IT) model with the lowest number of parameters. This type of Gemma model has low compute requirements and be able to respond to a wide variety of prompts without requiring additional development. Consider the following factors when choosing a Gemma variant: Gemma core, and other variant families such as PaliGemma, CodeGemma : Recommend Gemma (core). Gemma variants beyond the core version have the same architecture as the core model, and are trained to perform better at specific tasks. Unless your application or goals align with the specialization of a specific Gemma variant, it is best to start with a Gemma core, or base, model. Instruction-tuned (IT), pre-trained (PT), fine-tuned (FT), mixed (mix) : Recommend IT. Instruction-tuned (IT) Gemma variants are models that have been trained to respond to a variety of instructions or requests in human language. These model variants are the best place to start because they can respond to prompts without further model training. Pre-trained (PT) Gemma variants are models that have been trained to make inferences about language or other data, but have not been trained to follow human instructions. These models require additional training or tuning to be able to perform tasks effectively, and are meant for researchers or developers who want to study or develop the capabilities of the model and its architecture. Fine-tuned (FT) Gemma variants can be considered IT variants, but are typically trained to perform a specific task, or perform well on a specific generative AI benchmark. The PaliGemma variant family includes a number of FT variants. Mixed (mix) Gemma variants are versions of PaliGemma models that have been instruction tuned with a variety of instructions and are suitable for general use. Parameters : Recommend smallest number available . In general, the more parameters a model has, the more capable it is. However, running larger models requires larger and more complex compute resources, and generally slows down development of an AI application. Unless you have already determined that a smaller Gemma model cannot meet your needs, choose a one with a small number of parameters. Quantization levels: Recommend half precision (16-bit), except for tuning . Quantization is a complex topic that boils down to what size and precision of data, and consequently how much memory a generative AI model uses for calculations and generating responses. After a model is trained with high-precision data, which is typically 32-bit floating point data, models like Gemma can be modified to use lower precision data such as 16, 8 or 4-bit sizes. These quantized Gemma models can still perform well, depending on the complexity of the tasks, while using significantly less compute and memory resources. However, tools for tuning quantized models are limited and may not be available within your chosen AI development framework. Typically, you must fine-tune a model like Gemma at full precision, then quantize the resulting model. For a list of key, Google-published Gemma models, see the Getting started with Gemma models , Gemma model list. Run generation and inference requests After you have selected an AI execution framework and a Gemma variant, you can start running the model, and prompting it to generate content or complete tasks. For more information on how to run Gemma with a specific framework, see the guides linked in the Choose a framework section. Prompt formatting All instruction-tuned Gemma variants have specific prompt formatting requirements. Some of these formatting requirements are handled automatically by the framework you use to run Gemma models, but when you are sending prompt data directly to a tokenizer, you must add specific tags, and the tagging requirements can change depending on the Gemma variant you are using. Developed by Google DeepMind and other teams across Google, Gemma is named after the Latin gemma , meaning precious stone. The Gemma model weights are supported by developer tools that promote innovation, collaboration, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). You can get multiple variations of Gemma for general and specific use cases: Gemma 4 : Solve a wide variety of generative AI tasks with text, audio and image input, support for over 140 languages, and long 128K and up to 256K context window. EmbeddingGemma 2 : Produce numerical representations of text, images, audio, and video for downstream tasks like multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, and zero-shot classification. ShieldGemma 2 : Evaluate the safety of generative AI models' input and output against defined policies. Many more Gemma variants are available from Google and our AI developer community. Check them out on Kaggle Models and Hugging Face . Get inspired by what our community members have built with Gemma in the Gemmaverse . The Gemma models are available to run in your applications and on your hardware, mobile devices, or hosted services. You can also customize these models using tuning techniques so that they excel at performing specific tasks that matter to you and your users. Gemma models draw inspiration and technological lineage from the Gemini family of models, and are made for the AI development community to extend and take further. Ready to begin? Try it out . Home Gemini API Docs Send feedback Embeddings The Gemini API offers embedding models to generate embeddings for text, images, video, and other content. These resulting embeddings can then be used for tasks such as semantic search, classification, and clustering, providing more accurate, context-aware results than keyword-based approaches. The latest model, gemini-embedding-2 , is the first multimodal embedding model in the Gemini API. It maps text, images, video, audio, and documents into a unified embedding space, enabling cross-modal search, classification, and clustering across over 100 languages. See the multimodal embeddings section to learn more. For text-only use cases, gemini-embedding-001 remains available. Building Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems is a common use case for AI products. Embeddings play a key role in significantly enhancing model outputs with improved factual accuracy, coherence, and contextual richness. If you prefer to use a managed RAG solution, we built the File Search tool which makes doing RAG easier to manage and more cost effective. Generating embeddings Use the embedContent method to generate text embeddings: Python from google import genai client = genai . Println ( string ( embeddings )) } REST curl "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-embedding-2:embedContent" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-goog-api-key: ${ GEMINI_API_KEY } " \ -d '{ "model": "models/gemini-embedding-2", "content": { "parts": [{ "text": "What is the meaning of life?" }] } }' Note: While gemini-embedding-001 lets you generate individual embeddings for a list of strings, Gemini Embedding 2 produces a single aggregated embedding for multiple inputs. You can find more information in Embedding aggregation , or you can use the Batch API if you want to generate multiple embeddings at once. Specify task type to improve performance You can use embeddings for a wide range of tasks from classification to document search. Specifying the right task type helps optimize the embeddings for the intended relationships, maximizing accuracy and efficiency. Task types with Embeddings 2 For text-only tasks with gemini-embedding-2 , we strongly recommend you add the task instruction in your prompt. This can be done by formatting the query and the document with the correct task prefix. When generating a single embedding based on multimodal input , we generally don't recommend prefixing the text portion of the input with a task instruction. In some cases it improves performance, but in others it reduces performance. The following tables show examples of how to format queries and documents for symmetric and asymmetric use cases using the gemini-embedding-2 model. Retrieval use cases (Asymmetric format) In asymmetric use cases, add the task prefix to the query and apply the document structure for the content you want to embed and retrieve. Use case Query structure Document structure Search query task: search result | query: {content} title: {title} | text: {content} If there is no title, use title: none . Question answering task: question answering | query: {content} title: {title} | text: {content} Fact checking task: fact checking | query: {content} title: {title} | text: {content} Code retrieval task: code retrieval | query: {content} title: {title} | text: {content} Example usage Python # Generate embedding for a task's query. Use your correct task here: def prepare_query ( query ): # return f"task: question answering | query: {query}" # return f"task: fact checking | query: {query}" # return f"task: code retrieval | query: {query}" return f "task: search result | query: { query } " # Generate embedding for document of an asymmetric retrieval task: def prepare_document ( content , title = None ): if title is None : title = "none" return f "title: { title } | text: { content } " Single-input use cases (Symmetric format) In symmetric use cases, for the same task, use the same formatting for the query and the document. Use case Input structure Classification task: classification | query: {content} Clustering task: clustering | query: {content} Semantic similarity task: sentence similarity | query: {content} Do not use this for search or retrieval. It is intended for semantic textual similarity. Example usage Python # Generate embedding for query & document of your task. def prepare_query_and_document ( content ): # return f'task: clustering | query: {content}' # return f'task: sentence similarity | query: {content}' return f 'task: classification | query: { content } ' It is important that the task is used consistently. E.g., if documents are embedded with f'task: classification | query: {content}' , the query should also be embedded following this task format. Task types with Embeddings 1 For gemini-embedding-001 , you can specify the task_type in the embedContent method. For a complete list of supported task types, see the Supported task types table. Use FACT_VERIFICATION for the target text; RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT for documents to be retrieved Automated fact-checking systems Controlling embedding size Both gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-2 are trained using the Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) technique which teaches a model to learn high-dimensional embeddings that have initial segments (or prefixes) which are also useful, simpler versions of the same data. Use the output_dimensionality parameter to control the size of the output embedding vector. Selecting a smaller output dimensionality can save storage space and increase computational efficiency for downstream applications, while sacrificing little in terms of quality. By default, both models output a 3072-dimensional embedding, but you can truncate it to a smaller size without losing quality to save storage space. MRL Dimension MTEB Score (Gemini Embedding 001) 2048 68.16 1536 68.17 768 67.99 512 67.55 256 66.19 128 63.31 Multimodal embeddings The gemini-embedding-2 model supports multimodal input, allowing you to embed images, video, audio, and documents content alongside text. All modalities are mapped into the same embedding space, enabling cross-modal search and comparison. Supported modalities and limits The overall maximum input tokens limit is 8192 tokens. Embedding documents Documents in PDF format can be embedded directly. The model processes the visual and text content of each page. PDFs can be provided as inline data or as uploaded files through the Files API . How the model processes PDFs When you embed a PDF, the model processes the document using both visual and text features: Visual representation: The model renders each page as an image, which consumes 258 tokens per page. Text extraction: The model extracts text from the document. For native PDFs (which contain digital text), the model extracts the text directly. For scanned PDFs (which contain images of text), the model automatically runs optical character recognition (OCR) to extract the text. To calculate the total token count for a PDF, add the visual tokens (258 per page) to the text tokens. Your inputs must fit within the model's 8,192 token limit (shared across all modalities). Gemini Embedding 2 is Google's embedding generation model that's ideal for complex retrieval and analytics tasks. Gemini Embedding 2 accepts multimodal inputs to generate 3072-dimensional vectors. It accepts images, text, documents, audio, and video inputs and semantically maps the generated vectors into a unified semantic space. This lets you perform tasks, such as searching for an image based on a text description. Gemini Embedding 2 introduces several features to optimize embedding quality and flexibility: Custom task instructions: By specifying task instructions (for example, task:code retrieval or task:search result ) optimize the embeddings for the intended relationships and retrieve more accurate results for the specific goal. Adjustable result size: The model generates a 3072-dimensional float vector, by default. However, you can retrieve a smaller dimensional output by specifying the output_dimensionality parameter. Document OCR: Read OCR from document inputs. Audio track extraction: Extract audio tracks from video inputs and interleave them with video frames. For more information on how to use Gemini Embedding 2, see Get multimodal embeddings . We’re sharing Genie 4 in preview to learn alongside our community and safely advance the frontier of interactive simulation. Coherent environments Visual details and object permanence can shift or drift over time. This becomes more noticeable as a simulation runs longer, after multiple complex prompt edits, or when navigating throughout a scene. Interaction and simulation of other agents Accurately modeling complex interactions between users, multiple independent agents, and shared environments is an ongoing research challenge. Accurate representation of real-world locations Genie 4 is currently unable to simulate real-world locations with perfect accuracy. Text rendering Clear and legible text is often only generated when it's in the input world description. Limited interaction duration The model can support a few minutes of continuous interaction, rather than extended sessions. Audio accuracy Real-time audio accuracy remains an area of ongoing research and improvement. Responsibility Genie 4 marks a new area of frontier research that merges real-time generation and photorealism, introducing a new range of capabilities and dimensions that we want to roll out and explore in a responsible way. Genie 4 includes strict safety guardrails that are consistent with our safety policies across other models. Before launching this preview, we evaluated Genie 4 through internal rigorous safety evaluations to prevent the generation of harmful or malicious content. Also, we have intentionally deployed it first to trusted tester partners to get early feedback, before we release the model more broadly. To maintain transparency, all video and audio generated by Genie 4 will include SynthID, our imperceptible digital watermarking technology that helps identify AI-generated content across visual and audio modalities. What to think about while writing prompts The more detail you add, the more control you’ll have over the final output. Use a mix of the elements below to create results that better reflect your imagination. Shot framing and motion How do you want to frame your shot? Wide-angle, medium, or close-up? How do you want your camera to move? Should it glide gently, or rush suddenly? Experiment to find the right approach for your scene. Style How should your scene feel? Realistic, or cinematic? Grounded, or majestic? Tell Gemini Omni the effect you want to create, and leave the model to work out the details. Lighting How should your scene be lit? Where does the light come from – the sun, a streetlamp, or off-screen? What effect does it create? Is the lighting crisp, warm, or ethereal? Location Where is your scene set? Tell Gemini Omni the landscape you imagine – like “an alien landscape with clear, azure water”. But you don’t need to describe every single little detail, as Omni will work with your overall intention. Action What is happening in your scene? Who are the characters and objects? How are they moving and interacting? Edit through natural conversation Think of Gemini Omni like Nano Banana – but for video. Build and fine-tune your creation at any step with natural language. Edit iteratively Ask Gemini Omni for a specific update, like a background change or new caption, without needing to prompt your entire scene again. column5: How to create effective image prompts with Nano Banana — Google DeepMind Skip to main content Google DeepMind Build with Gemini Try Gemini Nano Banana How to create effective image prompts with Gemini Image Try in Gemini Try in Google AI Studio Prompt construction Editing with prompts General prompting What to think about while writing prompts Use detailed prompts to take more control over the images you generate. Think about what you want to see – the characters, the setting, and the overall feel. The more detail you add, the closer the image will be to what you’ve imagined. Style Are you creating an illustration, a photograph – or a watercolor painting? Do you want realistic characters, a retro-futuristic aesthetic, or something totally abstract? Subject Who, or what, is in your image? A human, an animal – something else entirely? What do they look like? What are they wearing? How are they posed? Setting Where does your scene take place? Is it a café on Mars, a cluttered alchemist’s library, or a sun-drenched meadow at golden hour? Action What’s happening? Is something falling? Floating? Is someone making a coffee, stroking a cat – or casting a magic spell? Composition How do you want to frame your shot? Portrait or landscape? Is it an extreme close-up, a wide shot, a low angle shot? Explore what works best. Editing with prompts After creating an image, you can keep editing it until you’re happy. Tweak specific details, reframe the image, upscale the quality – or overhaul the entire aesthetic. It’s up to you. Change the character Try swapping your subject for someone, or something, else. Or add extra characters – all while keeping the same style, setting, and composition. Adjust the composition Create new images from different angles, using the same subject and setting. And generate new details that are only visible from the new perspective. Alter the action Change what your characters are doing, to suit different situations. Do you want them to stand stand still, strike a fresh pose, or jump in the air? Swap the setting Transform the environment, as much or as little as you like. Change the entire backdrop, or swap out specific features and textures to fine-tune your setting. Rethink the style Freely reimagine the style of your composition. The model can reinterpret scenes, to switch between photographic style, illustrations, cartoons, and unique art styles. General prompting Even short prompts will generate high-quality images, but you can take better control of the output by adding details bit-by-bit. Keep playing, experimenting, and iterating, until you get the image you want to use. Visualize real-world knowledge Describe how you’d like the model to organize information by asking for a timeline or a flowchart. Prompt using real-world concepts, locations, or historical eras to draw from the model’s deep knowledge base. Mention the visual theme you’d like the design to follow. Render precise text Enclose your desired words in quotes (e.g., "Happy Birthday"). And describe the typography style, like a "bold sans-serif font" or "neon cursive signage". Translate and localize ideas Write in one language, then specify the target language and regional cultural cues in your prompt. If you need specific foreign phrasing, provide the exact translated text in quote marks to guide the rendering. Prompt for production-ready specs Prompt for your desired aspect ratio (like 4:3, 1:1, or 9:16) and describe the image format you need – for example, a "widescreen backdrop," or a "vertical social post". Look for the in-product resolution dropdowns to upscale to 2K or 4K. Ask for multiple images at once Ask for "three distinct variations of a product mock up" or "four different color palettes" to quickly compare ideas side-by-side. Or upload a single reference image and ask the model to generate a multi-image story based on it. Maintain subject consistency Upload clear reference images, and assign a distinct name to each character or object in your prompt. That way, the model can follow along and maintain their look as you build out your scenes. Nano Banana Imagine almost anything – then create it. Generate detailed, playful, realistic, or whimsical images. Or anything in-between. Try in Gemini Learn more about Nano Banana

How prompting in Lyria works Try in Gemini Simple prompts Get started with something basic. Request “a rock song” with a chosen lyrical theme and vocal style. Lyria will generate a track with instruments and vocals. Image-to-music prompts Upload an image to generate music to match. Try uploading holiday snaps, photos of your dog – or add a musical dimension to your visual art. Detailed, structured prompts Think about the tempo, dynamics, and instruments you want in your track. The more detail you add, the more control you have over the music. Prompt construction Prompting with images Prompting vocals and lyrics Experimenting with prompts What to think about while creating prompts Think about your genre, tempo, and the instruments you want to hear. Experiment by adding details to shape the mood and dynamics. Genre – or a mix of genres Pick a genre and era, like early 90s hip-hop, or 2000s pop. Or blend different genres within one song. Do you want a catchy K-pop tune with a Motown edge? Or merge classical violins into a funk track? It’s up to you. Tempo Ask for a fast or slow song. Or set a rough tempo by asking for a certain type of music – like a slow ballad, modern pop, or drum and bass. Instruments Add unexpected instruments into your chosen genre. “1950s jazz” will likely feature saxophones and trumpets. But you can add other instruments—like an 80s synth—to round out your sound. Or, if you don’t specify instruments, Lyria will automatically choose instruments to suit the genre. Dynamics Think about how music flows between sections. Maybe a quiet piano builds into an explosive chorus. Perhaps there’s an instrumental section. Or the vocals might get calmer and quieter as the track progresses. Prompting with images Upload images to capture their musical mood. Use your own photos and images, or create new ones with Nano Banana. Who’s in the image? Do they look happy or sad? What poses are they striking? What are they wearing? Are they human, animal, or alien? What’s the location? What can you see in the background? Inner city streets, or an exotic landscape? Are there people or wildlife in the background? What’s going on? Is it a posed family portrait? A hockey match? Or one man and his dog on a wilderness adventure? Lyria will interpret the setting to set the musical mood. Prompting vocals and lyrics Define your desired vocal style in detail. Share your own lyrics, or get help from Lyria by describing a theme. Create a vocal profile Do you want a male or female singer? Do they have commanding baritone vocals, or a clear and high soprano range? Is their voice rich, gravelly, soulful, breathy? And are they singing in English – or another language? Use your own lyrics Add specific lyrics by writing Lyrics: before the lines you’d like to hear. If you want backing singers to echo the main vocals, add that in round brackets. Like this: “ Lyrics: Let’s go (go) ”. Get lyrical help from Lyria If you want Lyria to generate lyrics for you, it’s best to make the theme clear with your prompt. You might want “a love song”, or “a song about success”. Or perhaps you want to write a “new happy birthday song” for your best friend. Experimenting with prompts Lyria can create a wide range of music – here are a few more ideas to explore. But these are only thought-starters – keep experimenting with your prompts to shape your tracks. Experimenting with musicality Prompt harmonies and counterpoints. Layer dense instrumental pieces – with unusual instruments. Keep trying new things, and see what Lyria creates for you. Experimenting with vocals Try describing specific vocal patterns you want to hear – like a “fast-paced”, or “laid-back” groove. Or you might want phrases or words repeated by backing vocals. See how you can layer different styles together. Experimenting with images Holiday snaps, or historical paintings. Friends, family – or your pet fish. Cartoons, illustrations, or scientific diagrams. Try out all sorts of images, to create all sorts of tracks. Lyria Explore new genres, play with soundscapes, and find musical inspiration. Prompt construction Environmental prompting Character prompting General prompting What to think about while creating prompts Prompting Genie 3 means thinking about three elements: the environment you want to build, the character you want to control, and the world sketch preview that sets out your world. You can prompt Genie 3 using text or images. Environment Describe the landscape you want to explore – from realistic to fantastic, cartoony to cinematic. Character Describe your character – a person, animal, object or something totally different. Explain how to direct it through your world – from walking to jumping, driving to flying. World Sketch Based on the environment and character prompts, Nano Banana Pro will generate an image preview of your world. Modify the image until it looks like the world you want to enter. You can also upload an image of your own. Environment prompting Build the world of your imagination Describe your environment Is it a forest, city, or mountain? Get specific about surfaces and terrain. Is it a dirt path? An asphalt road? A calm ocean? Describe the style of your environment Is it real world, game-like, cartoonish – or even built of nacho cheese? Describe what’s inside your environment List out any key structures, objects or additional characters. Is there a stone building with terracotta roofs? Temple ruins in the distance? A volcano on the horizon? Describe the way the environment behaves Include any specific movement you want to appear in your world. Is there wind? Does a dirt road release a dust cloud when your character walks on it? Are there objects that appear while you’re exploring? Character prompting Define your character and how it moves through its environment Describe the appearance or identity Be clear about who your character is and what it looks like. Is it a fluffy white rabbit? A microscopic ant? Robotic arms gripping the handlebars of a motorcycle? Detail primary actions, capabilities, and movement Describe what your character can do and how it moves. Is it capable of graceful flight? Does it drive forwards and backwards? Can it run and hop? Does it leave a trail of blue paint as it moves? Describe how your character’s movement affects the world Does the vehicle leave tracks in the dirt as it drives? Does the grass mower cut the grass as it moves through a field? General prompting Tips for building worlds Maintain direct, simple and action-oriented language Keep your descriptions to-the-point. Short declarative sentences work well. Evoke mood through strong sensory details Describe the way the environment and character feel to evoke the mood you want. Is the environment dimly lit with mysterious smoke on the ground? Does the character walk as if floating like a feather? Using game-like language can help build richer environments with more precise character control. Use Gemini to refine your prompt Use the Google Gemini app to rewrite, expand, and elaborate your descriptions. Fine-tune your world For text-only prompts, your image preview will inform the look of your world. Check it looks true to your idea, before you enter your world. Making worlds from your own images Uploading a high-quality image will yield the best results. Place your character in the center of the frame. Switch between first and third-person Click the perspective button to switch between a first-person and third-person view of the world. In third person, you’ll see your character. In first person, you’ll see the world through the eyes of your character.
