column5: Aeneas transforms how historians connect the past — Google DeepMind Skip to main content Google DeepMind Build with Gemini Try Gemini July 23, 2025 Research Aeneas transforms how historians connect the past The Aeneas team Share Introducing the first model for contextualizing ancient inscriptions, designed to help historians better interpret, attribute and restore fragmentary texts. Writing was everywhere in the Roman world — etched onto everything from imperial monuments to everyday objects. From political graffiti, love poems and epitaphs to business transactions, birthday invitations and magical spells, inscriptions offer modern historians rich insights into the diversity of everyday life across the Roman world. Often, these texts are fragmentary, weathered or deliberately defaced. Restoring, dating and placing them is nearly impossible without contextual information, especially when comparing similar inscriptions. Today, we’re publishing a paper in Nature introducing Aeneas , the first artificial intelligence (AI) model for contextualizing ancient inscriptions. When working with ancient inscriptions, historians traditionally rely on their expertise and specialized resources to identify “parallels” — which are texts that share similarities in wording, syntax, standardized formulas or provenance. Aeneas greatly accelerates this complex and time-consuming work. It reasons across thousands of Latin inscriptions, retrieving textual and contextual parallels in seconds that allow historians to interpret and build upon the model’s findings. Your browser does not support the video tag. Our model can also be adapted to other ancient languages, scripts and media, from papyri to coinage, expanding its capabilities to help draw connections across a wider range of historical evidence. We co-developed Aeneas with the University of Nottingham, and in partnership with researchers at the Universities of Warwick, Oxford and Athens University of Economics and Business (AUEB). This work was part of a wider effort to explore how generative AI can help historians better identify and interpret parallels at scale. We want this research to benefit as many people as possible, so we’re making an interactive version of Aeneas freely-available to researchers, students, educators, museum professionals and more at predictingthepast.com . To support further research, we’re also open-sourcing our code and dataset . Aeneas’ advanced capabilities Named after the wandering hero of Graeco-Roman mythology, Aeneas builds upon Ithaca , our earlier work using AI to restore, date and place ancient Greek inscriptions. Aeneas goes a step further, helping historians interpret and contextualize a text, give meaning to isolated fragments, draw richer conclusions and piece together a better understanding of ancient history. Our model’s advanced capabilities include: Parallels search: It searches for parallels across a vast collection of Latin inscriptions. By turning each text into a kind of historical fingerprint, Aeneas identifies deep connections that can help historians situate inscriptions within their broader historical context. Processing multimodal input: Aeneas is the first model to determine a text's geographical provenance using multimodal inputs. It analyzes both text and visual information, like images of an inscription. Restoring gaps of unknown length: For the first time, Aeneas can restore gaps in texts where the missing length is unknown. This makes it a more versatile tool for historians dealing with heavily damaged material. State-of-the-art performance: Aeneas sets a new state-of-the-art benchmark in restoring damaged texts and predicting when and where they were written. Animation of a restored bronze military diploma from Sardinia 113/14 C.E. ( CIL XVI, 60). How Aeneas works Aeneas is a multimodal generative neural network that takes an inscription’s text and image as input. To train Aeneas, we curated a large and reliable dataset, drawing from decades of work by historians to create digital collections, especially the Epigraphic Database Roma (EDR), Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (EDH) and Epigraphic Database Clauss Slaby (EDCS-ELT). We cleaned, harmonized and linked these records into a single machine-actionable dataset that we refer to as the Latin Epigraphic Dataset (LED), comprising over 176,000 Latin inscriptions from across the ancient Roman world. Our model uses a transformer-based decoder to process the textual input of an inscription. Specialized networks handle character restoration and dating using text, while geographical attribution also uses images of the inscriptions as input. The decoder retrieves similar inscriptions from the LED, ranked by relevance. For each inscription, Aeneas’ contextualization mechanism retrieves a list of parallels using a technique called “embeddings” — encoding the textual and contextual information of each inscription into a kind of historical fingerprint containing details of what the text says, its language, when and where it came from, and how it relates to other inscriptions. Diagram of Aeneas’ architecture showing how the model takes text and image input to generate province, date and restoration predictions. State-of-the-art performance Aeneas groups inscriptions by date of writing far more clearly than other general-purpose models also trained on Latin, as shown in the visualization below. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) visualization illustrating the chronological attribution of Aeneas’ historically rich embeddings compared to generic large language model textual embeddings. Aeneas restores damaged inscriptions with a Top-20 accuracy of 73% in gaps of up to ten characters. This only decreases to 58% when the restoration length is unknown - itself an incredibly challenging task. It also shows its reasoning in an interpretable way, providing saliency maps that highlight which parts of the inputs influenced its predictions. Thanks to its use of visual data, our model can attribute an inscription to one of 62 ancient Roman provinces with 72% accuracy. For dating, Aeneas places a text within 13 years of the date ranges provided by historians. A new lens on historical debates To test Aeneas’ capabilities on an ongoing research debate, we gave it one of the most famous Roman inscriptions: the Res Gestae Divi Augusti, Emperor Augustus’ first-person account of his achievements. Historians have long-argued about the dating of this inscription. Rather than predicting a single fixed date, Aeneas produced a detailed distribution of possible dates, showing two distinct peaks, with one smaller peak around 10-1 BCE and a larger, more confident peak between 10-20 CE. These results captured both prevailing dating hypotheses in a quantitative way. Histogram showing Aeneas’ chronological attribution prediction for the Res Gestae , which models scholarly debates around dating this famous inscription. Aeneas based its predictions on subtle linguistic features and historical markers such as official titles and monuments mentioned in the text. By turning the dating question into a probabilistic estimate grounded in linguistic and contextual data, our model offers a new, quantitative way of engaging with long-standing historical debates. Most importantly, Aeneas also retrieved many relevant parallels from imperial legal texts tied to Augustus’ legacy, highlighting how the ideology of empire was reproduced across media and geography. Advancing historical research collaboratively To assess Aeneas’ impact as an aid for research, we conducted a large-scale Historian and AI collaborative study. We invited twenty-three historians who regularly work with inscriptions to restore, date and place a set of texts using Aeneas. Our evaluation, summarized in the table below, shows how the most effective results were achieved when historians used Aeneas’ contextual information alongside its predictions for restoring and attributing Roman inscriptions. Table showing historians’ performance on three epigraphic tasks (restoration, geographical attribution, dating) using 60 inscriptions from our database test set. Tasks were first performed independently, then with Aeneas’ parallels information, or parallels and predictions together. Aeneas helped the historians in our study identify new parallels and increased their confidence when tackling complex epigraphic tasks. Historians consistently highlighted Aeneas’ value in accelerating their work and expanding the range of most relevant parallel inscriptions. Aeneas’ parallels completely changed my perception of the inscription. It noticed details that made all the difference for restoring and chronologically attributing the text. Anonymised historian from our study Sharing the tools, shaping the future Aeneas is designed to integrate within historians' existing research workflows. By combining expert knowledge with machine learning, it opens up a collaborative process, offering interpretable suggestions that serve as valuable starting points for historical inquiry. As part of today’s release, we’re upgrading Ithaca , our ancient Greek model, to be powered by Aeneas and include the contextualization function, restorations of unknown length and better performance overall. We’ve also co-designed a new teaching syllabus for bridging technical skills with historical thinking in the classroom. This syllabus aligns with AI literacy initiatives, including the European Commission's Digital Competences Framework for Citizens (DigComp 2.2), UNESCO’s AI Competency Framework for Students , and the preview of European Commission and the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) AILit Framework . The Aeneas team is continuing to partner with diverse subject matter experts, using Aeneas to help shed light to our ancient past — with more to come. The Aeneas web interface was developed by Justin Grayston, Benjamin Maynard, and Nicholas Dietrich, and is powered by Google Cloud. column4: How Google Research created its ZAPBench brain mapping dataset
column5: How Google Research created its ZAPBench brain mapping dataset How we built one of the most ambitious datasets in brain activity research Jun 09, 2025 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link ZAPBench predicts and shows neural activity of larval zebrafish — which could lead to major breakthroughs for how we understand our own brains. Chaim Gartenberg Contributor Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link National Institute of Genetics For almost a decade, Michał Januszewski has been thinking about what fish are thinking about. Michał is part of Google Research, which has been working with collaborators at HHMI Janelia and Harvard University to build one of the most ambitious datasets in brain activity research yet: a dataset that tracks both the neural activity and nanoscale structure of an entire brain of single larval zebrafish — which could lead to major breakthroughs for how we understand our own brains. “For years, our team has been really focusing on what’s called connectomics, which deals with the structural mapping of brains — we take very high-resolution pictures of small fragments of brains and try to identify all cells and all the connections between them,” Michał says. “That gives you a static snapshot of the brain as it is at any given moment in time, but doesn’t tell you what the brain is doing when it's actually alive and thinking.” So Michał's team looked to build a new, multimodal dataset that could predict and show neural activity of an organism as it thinks. They chose to start with the zebrafish, which checked several key boxes: It is a vertebrate animal, with more complex brain functions than, say, an insect, and its brain is small enough that the team could get a dataset of the entire brain, instead of just a tiny portion of it. And — perhaps most importantly — newly hatched zebrafish are almost entirely transparent, allowing the team to use a specialized laser rig to scan nearly two hours of brain activity for more than 70,000 neurons in a live fish’s brain as it reacts to various patterns and stimuli being projected around it. In April, Google Research released that data as a first-of-its-kind benchmark, called ZAPBench (Zebrafish Activity Prediction Benchmark), which can help advance neuroscience by enabling the development of more accurate AI models that can predict brain activity. Researchers used a light sheet microscope to record brain activity in a larval zebrafish. Researchers at Google have created plenty of AI model benchmarks to drive improvements for models in other fields, like WeatherBench 2 for improving forecasts, or the One Billion Word Benchmark for language models. ZAPBench, however, fills a unique need. While it can be easy to double check the accuracy of something like a weather prediction from an AI model by, say, sticking your head out a window, there’s no simple way to test predictive models for brain activity, due to the difficulty in obtaining scan data in the first place. “Neuroscience researchers have been building models for how the brain works, but it's been relatively rare to be able to put them to the test for how well they can actually predict brain activity,” says Research Scientist Viren Jain. ”With ZAPBench, anybody can create models and evaluate them, both against the benchmark and other models.” The team at Google has already seen some interesting results in their own tests, including how models tended to make mistakes in predictions in specific areas of the brain, but were more accurate at predicting activity in others. The originally recorded brain activity data (left), and a predicted brain activity image that ZAPBench is able to help benchmark (right). Creating ZAPBench is just the first step. The Google Research team is also building on its existing work to map the connectome of the tens of thousands of neurons of the exact same larval zebrafish brain whose activity was imaged. The hope is that by pairing the connectome of the specific specimen’s brain together with the activity of that brain, we’ll be able to find new insights into how brains work on a basic level — both for fish, and one day, even for humans. “The long-term goal here is to figure out how the brain operates at a really mechanistic level,” Viren says. “And if we can develop a model that’s better at predicting how all these different components drive brain activity, it’ll significantly advance the state of and our confidence in basic models of how the brain works — which could drive applications in medicine, brain computer interfaces or any number of helpful applications in the future.” Posted in: Related stories Learning & Education Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain By Ronit Levavi Morad Google Research How Google Beam connects military families globally By Josh Woodward Google Research Ask a Scientist: How can AI help doctors spend more time on collaborative care? column4: AlphaProteo generates novel proteins for biology and health research — Google DeepMind
column5: AlphaProteo generates novel proteins for biology and health research — Google DeepMind Skip to main content Google DeepMind Build with Gemini Try Gemini September 5, 2024 Science AlphaProteo generates novel proteins for biology and health research Protein Design and Wet Lab teams Share New AI system designs proteins that successfully bind to target molecules, with potential for advancing drug design, disease understanding and more. Every biological process in the body, from cell growth to immune responses, depends on interactions between molecules called proteins. Like a key to a lock, one protein can bind to another, helping regulate critical cellular processes. Protein structure prediction tools like AlphaFold have already given us tremendous insight into how proteins interact with each other to perform their functions, but these tools cannot create new proteins to directly manipulate those interactions. Scientists, however, can create novel proteins that successfully bind to target molecules. These binders can help researchers accelerate progress across a broad spectrum of research, including drug development, cell and tissue imaging, disease understanding and diagnosis – even crop resistance to pests. While recent machine learning approaches to protein design have made great strides, the process is still laborious and requires extensive experimental testing. Today, we introduce AlphaProteo , our first AI system for designing novel, high-strength protein binders to serve as building blocks for biological and health research. This technology has the potential to accelerate our understanding of biological processes, and aid the discovery of new drugs, the development of biosensors and more. AlphaProteo can generate new protein binders for diverse target proteins, including VEGF-A , which is associated with cancer and complications from diabetes. This is the first time an AI tool has been able to design a successful protein binder for VEGF-A. AlphaProteo also achieves higher experimental success rates and 3 to 300 times better binding affinities than the best existing methods on seven target proteins we tested. Learning the intricate ways proteins bind to each other Protein binders that can bind tightly to a target protein are hard to design. Traditional methods are time intensive, requiring multiple rounds of extensive lab work. After the binders are created, they undergo additional experimental rounds to optimize binding affinity, so they bind tightly enough to be useful. Trained on large amounts of protein data from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) and more than 100 million predicted structures from AlphaFold, AlphaProteo has learned the myriad ways molecules bind to each other. Given the structure of a target molecule and a set of preferred binding locations on that molecule, AlphaProteo generates a candidate protein that binds to the target at those locations. Your browser does not support the video tag. Illustration of a predicted protein binder structure interacting with a target protein. Shown in blue is a predicted protein binder structure generated by AlphaProteo, designed for binding to a target protein. Shown in yellow is the target protein, specifically the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain Demonstrating success on important protein binding targets To test AlphaProteo, we designed binders for diverse target proteins, including two viral proteins involved in infection, BHRF1 and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain, SC2RBD, and five proteins involved in cancer, inflammation and autoimmune diseases, IL-7Rɑ , PD-L1 , TrkA , IL-17A and VEGF-A . Our system has highly-competitive binding success rates and best-in-class binding strengths. For seven targets, AlphaProteo generated candidate proteins in-silico that bound strongly to their intended proteins when tested experimentally. A grid of illustrations of predicted structures of seven target proteins for which AlphaProteo generated successful binders. Shown in blue are examples of binders tested in the wet lab, shown in yellow are protein targets, and highlighted in dark yellow are intended binding regions. For one particular target, the viral protein BHRF1 , 88% of our candidate molecules bound successfully when tested in the Google DeepMind Wet Lab . Based on the targets tested, AlphaProteo binders also bind 10 times more strongly, on average, than the best existing design methods. For another target, TrkA , our binders are even stronger than the best prior designed binders to this target that have been through multiple rounds of experimental optimization . Bar graph showing experimental in vitro success rates of AlphaProteo’s output for each of the seven target proteins, compared to other design methods. Higher success rates mean fewer designs must be tested to find successful binders. Bar graph showing the best affinity for AlphaProteo’s designs without experimental optimization for each of the seven target proteins, compared to other design methods. Lower affinity means the binder protein binds more tightly to the target protein. Please note the logarithmic scale of the vertical axis. Validating our results Beyond in silico validation and testing AlphaProteo in our wet lab, we engaged Peter Cherepanov’s , Katie Bentley’s and David LV Bauer’s research groups from the Francis Crick Institute to validate our protein binders. Across different experiments, they dived deeper into some of our stronger SC2RBD and VEGF-A binders. The research groups confirmed that the binding interactions of these binders were indeed similar to what AlphaProteo had predicted. Additionally, the groups confirmed that the binders have useful biological function. For example, some of our SC2RBD binders were shown to prevent SARS-CoV-2 and some of its variants from infecting cells. AlphaProteo’s performance indicates that it could drastically reduce the time needed for initial experiments involving protein binders for a broad range of applications. However, we know that our AI system has limitations, as it was unable to design successful binders against an 8th target, TNFɑ , a protein associated with autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis. We selected TNFɑ to robustly challenge AlphaProteo, as computational analysis showed that it would be extremely difficult to design binders against. We will continue to improve and expand AlphaProteo's capabilities with the goal of eventually addressing such challenging targets. Achieving strong binding is usually only the first step in designing proteins that might be useful for practical applications, and there are many more bioengineering obstacles to overcome in the research and development process. Towards responsible development of protein design Protein design is a fast-evolving technology that holds lots of potential for advancing science in everything from understanding the factors that cause disease, to accelerating diagnostic test development for virus outbreaks, supporting more sustainable manufacturing processes, and even cleaning contaminants from the environment. To account for potential risks in biosecurity, building on our long-standing approach to responsibility and safety, we’re working with leading external experts to inform our phased approach to sharing this work, and feeding into community efforts to develop best practices, including the NTI’ s (Nuclear Threat Initiative) new AI Bio Forum . Going forward, we’ll be working with the scientific community to leverage AlphaProteo on impactful biology problems and understand its limitations. We've also been exploring its drug design applications at Isomorphic Labs, and are excited for what the future holds. At the same time, we’re continuing to improve the success rate and affinity of AlphaProteo’s algorithms, expanding the range of design problems it can tackle, and working with researchers in machine learning, structural biology, biochemistry and other disciplines to develop a responsible and more comprehensive protein design offering for the community. Read our whitepaper Acknowledgements This research was co-developed by our Protein Design team and Wet Lab team. We’d like to thank our collaborators Peter Cherepanov, David Bauer, Katie Bentley and their groups at the Francis Crick Institute for their invaluable experimental insights and results, the AlphaFold team, whose earlier work and algorithms provided training inputs and evaluation insights, and the many other teams across Google DeepMind who contributed to this program. Download AlphaFold 3 Explore the latest AlphaFold has revealed millions of intricate 3D protein structures, and is helping scientists understand how life’s molecules interact. What is AlphaFold? AlphaFold's impact Case studies Try AlphaFold What is AlphaFold? Proteins underpin every biological process, in every living thing. Made from long chains of amino acids, each has a unique complex 3D structure. But figuring out just one of these can take several years, and hundreds of thousands of dollars. In 2020, AlphaFold solved this problem, with the ability to predict protein structures in minutes, to a remarkable degree of accuracy. That’s helping researchers understand what individual proteins do and how they interact with other molecules. So valuable time and resources can be redirected into advancing research that could help solve society’s biggest medical and environmental challenges. Timeline of a breakthrough In November 2020, AlphaFold was recognised as a solution to the 50-year “protein-folding problem”. Slide 1 of 9 13th March 2016 AlphaGo’s success proves AI’s readiness to tackle protein folding DeepMind’s AlphaGo program defeats legendary Go player Lee Sae Dol in a challenge match in Seoul. This watershed moment demonstrated that DeepMind’s AI techniques were potentially advanced enough to be applied to scientific challenges. A small team is established to start working on protein structure prediction. 2nd December 2018 AlphaFold places first at CASP13 AlphaFold’s performance is benchmarked in the 13th Critical Assessment of Protein Structure Prediction (CASP13), placing first in the rankings (under entry A7D). The methods are subsequently published in the scientific journal Nature . The team is expanded, and work begins on an innovative new system. 30th November 2020 AlphaFold is recognised as a solution to the protein folding problem at CASP14 AlphaFold2 wins CASP14 by a huge margin and is recognised as a solution to the 50-year-old “protein folding problem” by the organisers of CASP after predicting structures down to atomic accuracy with a median error (RMSD_95) of less than 1 Angstrom - 3 times more accurate than the next best system and comparable to experimental methods. 15th July 2021 AlphaFold’s methodology is published in Nature Nature publishes AlphaFold’s detailed methodology in the paper “ Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold ” and DeepMind open sources the code along with 60 pages of supplemental information. To-date, the paper has been cited over 40,000 times in scientific journals. 22nd July 2021 We launch the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with EMBL-EB A week later, Nature publishes a second DeepMind paper containing the structure predictions of the entire human proteome. In close collaboration with the European Bioinformatics Institute at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL-EBI), DeepMind launches the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (AFDB) to give the scientific community free of charge and open access to the human proteome along with another 20 model organisms - over 350,000 structures in total. 28th July 2022 We share the structures of over 200 million proteins with the research community In partnership with EMBL’s European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI) , DeepMind releases the predicted structures for nearly all catalogued proteins known to science, expanding the AFDB to over 200 million structures. 8th May 2024 AlphaFold 3 and AlphaFold Server are launched Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs introduce AlphaFold 3 , which predicts the structure and interactions of all of life’s molecules. At the same time, Google DeepMind launches AlphaFold Server , a platform that provides scientists free access to AF3 structure prediction capabilities for non-commercial research. 9th October 2024 AlphaFold is recognised by the Nobel Committee Demis Hassabis and John Jumper are co-awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work on AlphaFold, alongside David Baker for his work on computational protein design. November 2025 AlphaFold is a global research tool AlphaFold is being used by over 3 million researchers from over 190 countries around the world, tackling problems such as antimicrobial resistance, crop resilience and heart disease. What took us months and years to do, AlphaFold was able to do in a weekend. Professor John McGeehan Former Director for the Centre for Enzyme Innovation (CEI) Over 2 million researchers in over 190 countries are using the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database to inform their research. Slide 1 of 2 Managing plastic pollution 91% of all plastic ever produced has never been recycled. AlphaFold could help us face up to the challenge of cleaning up our world. Supporting global food supplies 40% of the world’s crops are lost to disease each year. AlphaFold could unlock insights that help keep food on tables. AlphaFold’s impact AlphaFold has already made a significant impact. We hope it will eventually help to transform our understanding of the biological world. So far, AlphaFold has predicted over 200 million protein structures – nearly all catalogued proteins known to science. The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database makes this data freely available. So far, it has over three million users from over 190 countries. That means it has already potentially saved millions of dollars and hundreds of millions of years in research time. Meanwhile, AlphaFold Server predicts how proteins will interact with a broad spectrum of biomolecules, accelerating new research. Hundreds of millions Research years saved by AlphaFold database structures. Over 1 million Users in low and middle income countries. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Tens of millions of small business owners are using Gemini today to brainstorm future products, manage customer feedback, and analyze business performance. Today, we’re announcing new tools designed to give these entrepreneurs their time back so they can focus on what started it all: their passion. A central hub for small businesses owners, all in Gemini We’re introducing a new business landing page designed to help small business owners streamline their daily tasks. From this central hub, they can build their brand, analyze finances, understand customer insights, and more. We’re also making it easy to connect Gemini to Google tools like Google Business Profile, Google Ads, and Google Workspace, as well as third-party connected apps like Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho, and Xero. On-brand visuals Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading their website, brand kit, fonts, or color palettes. column4: Guided Vision launches in Gemini Live for Android
column5: Guided Vision launches in Gemini Live for Android Guided Vision in Gemini Live: built for accessibility Oct 01, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Built alongside the blind and low-vision community, Guided Vision in Gemini Live offers conversational, real-time visual assistance. Share your camera to receive dynamic audio descriptions and natural verbal reframing cues to explore your environment. Isha Sheth Senior Product Manager, Gemini Live Scott Adams Senior Product Manager, Google Accessibility Engineering Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Today, we’re launching Guided Vision in Gemini Live across compatible Android devices — bringing voice-forward, real-time visual interpretation to people who are blind, have low vision, or want intuitive visual assistance. Technology is most powerful when it opens up the world for everyone, and Guided Vision turns Gemini into a conversational visual partner. Guided Vision was developed through close collaboration with the accessibility community. We previewed it earlier this month, among other tools to expand digital and physical accessibility across Android. To train Gemini Live for conversational, real-world context, we partnered with Aira to visually interpret data for a total of tens of thousands of hours. More than 1,000 members of Aira’s Trusted Tester network helped stress-test and refine the model across daily routines, while Aira specialists worked directly with our teams as subject-matter experts to help establish and evaluate our safety guardrails. Now, you can simply share your camera during a Gemini Live session to hear clear descriptions of your surroundings, ask detailed follow-up questions, and receive proactive, spoken cues to center whatever you want to explore. Real-time visual assistance designed for how you experience the world When you share your camera in Gemini Live with Guided Vision turned on, Gemini acts as a conversational partner. If your camera is pointed too high, too close, or slightly off to the side, Gemini provides natural verbal prompts to help you reframe — asking you to pan slowly to the right, tilt downward, or step back so it can get the clear visual context needed to answer your questions. Everyday moments made simple Whether locating objects, preparing a meal, or picking an outfit, Guided Vision supports everyday tasks where quick visual verification matters most: Reading fine print and complex text : Read small nutrition labels on food packages, decipher appliance dials and washing machine cycles, or read printed menus in dimly lit restaurants. Finding and locating objects: Search your immediate area for everyday items, such as finding a dropped earbud on the floor or locating the black pepper inside a crowded spice cabinet. Describing objects and matching details: Ask about colors, patterns, and shapes — such as checking whether a striped shirt pairs with a pair of trousers or identifying the color of a specific jacket. Exploring your immediate environment : Get descriptive overviews of unfamiliar spaces, room layouts, or objects placed across a table. Conversing naturally in your preferred language: Guided Vision supports conversations across multiple languages. It reflects extensive testing and feedback from blind and low-vision communities across India, Brazil, Singapore, Indonesia, Japan, and more to make descriptions, reframing cues, and answers feel natural and helpful. Like many accessibility innovations, Guided Vision also provides practical visual assistance for older adults, individuals with low literacy, or anyone trying to read fine print in low lighting. Quick access across Android Guided Vision is designed to fit seamlessly into daily routines with minimal friction: Gemini App : Open your profile settings in the Gemini mobile app and switch on Use Guided Vision in Live . From there, open Gemini Live and tap to share your camera. Accessibility Shortcuts : Under Android Settings > Accessibility > Vision assistance > Guided Vision, configure an Accessibility shortcut to launch Guided Vision using the floating accessibility button, a two-finger swipe gesture, or by pressing both volume keys. TalkBack Integration : Users running Google TalkBack can bring up the TalkBack menu with a three-finger tap and select Guided Vision directly. As with any generative AI technology, Guided Vision is an assistive utility and can make mistakes. It is not a medical device, mobility aid, or white cane replacement, and it’s not intended for navigation, safe-travel guidance, or obstacle detection. Users should continue relying on established mobility aids and safe-travel practices in physical environments. Guided Vision is now available on Android devices running Android 9 and above in regions and languages where Gemini Live is supported. Make sure your Gemini app and Android system software are updated to the latest versions to get started. News and Events YouTube Music adds new labels for AI music Oct 14, 2026 Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music. As these tools evolve, our listeners have told us they want transparency when they’re hearing an AI-generated track. Starting today, YouTube Music is rolling out labels to make it easier to see when a song was created primarily using generative AI. For example, this includes using a generative model to create the composition and vocals. These new music labels will also expand to the main YouTube app. Clear labels right on the player When you listen to a track on YouTube Music where AI played a significant role, you’ll see a label directly on the player page. Tapping the label opens a simple menu that shares more information. We’re teaming up with music partners and using our own detection tools to identify AI-generated tracks, applying the same labeling principles already used across YouTube. Our goal is to make it as easy as possible for viewers and listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to. column4: Copyright tools: Rightsholders and creators - How YouTube Works
column5: Copyright tools: Rightsholders and creators - How YouTube Works Jump to content Copyright YouTube is designed to ensure that every player in our ecosystem can be successful. This includes both protecting rightsholders and giving creators peace of mind so that they can focus on producing original content. Copyright protection tools Copyright claims appeals How YouTube’s Copyright Protection Tools work We've invested millions of dollars in developing a Copyright Management Suite that's designed to balance the needs of our entire ecosystem — and we have clear rules when it comes to copyright. YouTube has worked directly with rightsholders to ensure that copyrighted material on our platform is authorised, and that we provide those robust tools to allow rightsholders to notify YouTube of alleged infringement, which we remove in accordance with the law. There are three main tools that make up our Copyright Management Suite: Webform Who is it for? Available in more than 80 languages, all rightsholders have access to the webform, which we've built as a streamlined and efficient way to submit copyright removal requests. What does it do? Rightsholders enter a few details of their request, which is then reviewed by YouTube to see if it meets the legal requirements for removing the reported content. Rights holders have access to powerful features, including the ability to ask YouTube to automatically prevent copies of the removed content from being reuploaded. Copyright Match Tool Who’s it for? It helps creators and rights holders protect their content by automatically finding videos that are the same or very similar to ones previously uploaded. What does it do? If a match is found, the creator or the rightsholder is notified. They can then review the video that potentially reused their content and decide whether to request the video's removal. Content ID Who's it for? Rightsholders who have the most complex rights management needs and experience heavy reposting of copyrighted material, like film studios and music labels. What does it do? Rightsholders can pre-determine rules for when content matches are found, choosing to block a whole video from being viewed, monetise the video by running ads against it or track the video's viewership stats. column5: YouTube Policies Crafted for Openness - How YouTube Works Jump to content Our Policies YouTube’s mission is to give everyone a voice and show them the world — and openness and free expression are at the heart of this. Our platform is a place where a broad range of perspectives are encouraged, and we don’t shy away from disagreement and debate. How our guidelines work How we support creators Combating abuse How Community & Ad-Friendly Guidelines work Our policies help us maintain a responsible business that viewers, creators, and advertisers can rely on in order to continue to thrive on YouTube. As with any system, we sometimes make mistakes. That’s why appeals are an important part of our processes. Creators are notified when their videos are removed due to policy violations or when they may be suspended from YPP, and can appeal if they disagree with our decision. Our Community Guidelines and Advertiser-Friendly Content Guidelines are what enable us to strike this balance. Community Guidelines Content that violates our community guidelines is flagged by a mix of automated detection and human reporting — most is automatically detected — and we go to great lengths to make sure violative content isn’t widely viewed, or even viewed at all, before it’s taken down. Exceptions can be made when content has a clear educational, documentary, scientific, or artistic (EDSA) context, including content that is in the public’s interest. Advertiser-Friendly Content Guidelines Brands rely on us to protect their business interests when they’re advertising on YouTube. To help support this, we have a set of Ad-Friendly guidelines creators in the YouTube Partner Program (YPP) need to follow in order to have Ads served on their channel content and earn a share of the revenue. How we support creators Since 2007, we’ve been paying eligible creators every month through our revenue-sharing model, the YouTube Partner Program . For a creator to be eligible for YPP, they must meet a higher bar for what they share on YouTube. Creators have to follow YouTube monetization policies and we review each applicant’s channel before admitting them to YPP. We also demonetize videos that violate our Advertiser Friendly Guidelines, and suspend creators from YPP for repeat offenses. With this model, creators have a long-term incentive to reinforce YouTube’s safety and follow our policies. We also provide Creators with an array of tools to manage their content & communities: Manage Experiences Channel Guidelines help creators set what kind of conversations they want to have on their channel. Creators can hold potentially inappropriate comments for review, hide certain individuals, block words, assign moderation privileges, and more. How to set channel guidelines Channel Management We provide creators with an array of products that help them decide how to manage their channels. How to manage posts and comments Privacy & Safety Resources The privacy and safety of creators on YouTube is important to us, and we provide a range of tools & resources to support them. How to use privacy and safety tools How YouTube Partners with Industry Experts to Combat Abuse Content that’s meant to praise, promote, or aid violent extremist or criminal organizations is not allowed on YouTube. We rely on many factors — like certain government and international organization designations — to determine what constitutes criminal or terrorist organizations. We’re also a founding member of the Global Internet Forum to Counter Terrorism (GIFCT) , where we work with other tech companies to keep terrorist content off the web — and provide training and other resources to smaller companies facing similar challenges. column5: À propos de Google au Canada - About Google around the world Accéder au contenu Depuis 25 ans, Google est fière d’exercer ses activités au Canada. Face à l'avenir, nous demeurons déterminés à ouvrir la voie à une nouvelle ère d'innovation, avec le Canada à l'avant-plan. Notre impact Aider les Canadiens à prospérer Renforcer l’économie canadienne Soutenir l’innovation gouvernementale Play animation Pause animation Notre impact au Canada Plus de 81 G$ En 2025, Recherche Google, Google Play, YouTube, Google Cloud et les outils de publicité de Google ont contribué à l’activité économique à hauteur de 81 milliards de dollars pour ales entreprises, les organismes à but non lucratif, les éditeurs, les créateurs et les développeurs canadiens. Plus de 2,8 M En 2025, plus de 2,8 millions d’entreprises canadiennes utilisaient des outils de Google sans frais pour gérer et développer leur entreprise. Plus de 1 million Depuis 2017, Google a aidé plus de 1 million de Canadiens à acquérir des compétences en informatique et en IA pour profiter des débouchés créés par la technologie. Plus de 1,3 G$ Depuis 2009, Google et ses employés ont offert plus de 1,3 milliard de dollars en financement (subventions en espèces, fonds à impact social, dons d’employés et contributions jumelées) à des organisations et à des organismes à but non lucratif au pays. Rapport d’impact économique de Google au Canada Découvrez notre impact à l’échelle du pays. Publié en 2026. En savoir plus Contribuer à la prospérité des Canadiens Nous voulons aider les Canadiens à accéder aux avantages de l’IA. Depuis plus de 10 ans, nous intégrons l’IA à nos produits et faisons évoluer la recherche scientifique pour le quotidien et réaliser des percées qui élargissent les possibilités. L’IA de Google marque une nouvelle ère d’innovation au Canada Link to Youtube Video (visible only when JS is disabled) Grâce au soutien de Google.org, la Toronto Public Library propose une formation sans fraissur l’IA Avec le soutien de Google.org, la Toronto Public Library s’attaque au fossé numérique grâce à une initiative de développement des compétences en IA à l’échelle de la ville. Offrant aux résidents un accès gratuit à des outils et à des formations sur l’IA, sa programmation soutient la recherche d’emploi, le gain de productivité et l’utilisation sécuritaire et éclairée de l’IA. CropMind aide les agriculteurs à augmenter les rendements grâce à l’IA de Google Les variations climatiques et météorologiques peuvent avoir de grandes répercussions sur les cultures agricoles. Propulsée par l’IA de Google, la plateforme de CropMind fournit de l’information pertinente et précise dès le début sur la santé des cultures, aidant ainsi les agriculteurs à protéger leurs récoltes et à augmenter les rendements. Skills for Change trace de nouveaux chemins vers des emplois valorisants grâce à Grow with Google Avec le soutien de Google.org, Skills for Change aide les groupes sociaux mal desservis, comme les femmes, les nouveaux arrivants, les personnes racisées et les jeunes, à développer leur littératie en IA et à tracer de nouveaux chemins vers des emplois valorisants. Livestock Water Recycling (LWR) aide les agriculteurs à réduire les émissions grâce à l’IA de Google Avec l’aide de l’IA de Google, LWR transforme les pratiques de gestion des déchets d’élevage. Ses installations agricoles utilisent l’IA de Google pour convertir les matières résiduelles en engrais tout en aidant les agriculteurs à éliminer les gaz à effet de serre, à rentabiliser davantage leurs exploitations agricoles et à augmenter leurs profits. Sachin Jaiswal entame une carrière en cybersécurité spécialisée grâce au Certificat de carrière en cybersécurité de Google Installé à Winnipeg depuis son départ de l’Inde, Sachin Jaiswal occupait un poste dans le soutien informatique lorsqu’un problème de permis de travail a mis fin à son emploi. Grâce à une bourse accordée par ComIT, un partenaire de Grow with Google, Sachin s’est inscrit au Certificat de carrière en cybersécurité de Google. Ce certificat a donné à Sachin le coup de pouce dont il avait besoin pour se démarquer dans un marché très concurrentiel. GoBolt augmente ses livraisons et réduit ses émissions à l’aide de l’IA de Google La hausse du nombre de livraisons de paquets au pays entraîne une augmentation des émissions de carbone. Afin de réduire son empreinte carbone, GoBolt utilise l’IA de Google pour optimiser ses trajets et livrer plus de paquets avec moins de véhicules AccessNow cartographie les espaces accessibles au Canada à l’aide de l’IA de Google Les personnes handicapées font face à des obstacles lors de leurs déplacements. Avec l’IA de Google, la plateforme d’AccessNow cartographie les endroits accessibles, détermine les obstacles et aide à concevoir des espaces plus inclusifs. Une entrepreneure accélère son apprentissage de l’IA grâce au Certificat de carrière de Google sur l’IA Icy Mountain Water Co., une petite entreprise familiale indépendante, est en activité depuis 1992 à Medicine Hat, en Alberta, et Brandy Wilde y porte à peu près tous les chapeaux. Déterminée à faire grandir son entreprise familiale, Brandy s’est inscrite au Certificat de carrière sur l’IA de Grow with Google. En utilisant l’IA pour accomplir certaines tâches de son quotidien, elle a désormais la marge de manœuvre nécessaire pour se consacrer à sa croissance et au développement de partenariats locaux. 1 / Renforcer l’économie canadienne L’IA renforce l’économie canadienne en aidant entreprises et employés (résolution de problèmes, gain de temps, réalisations avec leurs ressources). En utilisant le Profil d’entreprise de Google pour partager des avis authentiques, la fondatrice Katrina Wood a su transformer les recherches en ligne en de vrais liens communautaires; en un seul mois, elle a augmenté le nombre de vues de 11 % et généré plus de 700 interactions directes avec la clientèle. Red Barn Brewing mise sur l’IA de Google pour faire mousser sa croissance Pour Red Barn Brewing, gérer à la fois les processus et les évènements créait souvent des goulots d’étranglement. Avec l’aide de Gemini, le copropriétaire Denny a créé une appli sur mesure pour centraliser ses opérations, réduisant ainsi le temps consacré aux tâches administratives et aidant son équipe à faire preuve de plus d’agilité. Destination Canada accroît le tourisme local avec l’aide de l’IA de Google Le tourisme est un moteur crucial de l’économie du pays. La plateforme de Destination Canada, propulsée par l’IA de Google, offre des données pour aider entreprises et gouvernements (décisions, hausse de revenus et soutien des communautés locales). Eco-Coffee, une entreprise de Kitchener, utilise Gemini et Firebase pour créer des applis d’entretien et de calcul des coûts en temps réel, automatisant ainsi les tâches chronophages afin de pouvoir se consacrer à la croissance de l’entreprise. The Overthinkers Club encourage l’entrepreneuriat chez les personnes neurodivergentes grâce à l’IA de Google Gérer le quotidien d’une entreprise peut représenter un défi de taille pour les fondateurs neuroatypiques. Marissa, la fondatrice de The Overthinkers Club, utilise Gemini en tant que partenaire collaboratif pour organiser ses pensées, tout en stimulant sa productivité, mais sans jamais brusquer le rythme naturel de ses pensées. Flare Events utilise Gemini et Google Cloud pour coordonner plus de 400 évènements par année dans huit villes canadiennes, ce qui lui permet d’alléger son fardeau administratif, de protéger les renseignements de ses membres et de cultiver de véritables liens humains. Pour ces petits établissements, rivaliser avec de grandes chaînes hôtelières représente un énorme défi. Le gîte Craigleith Manor, à Collingwood en Ontario, utilise Gemini et Google Hotel Ads pour optimiser ses campagnes publicitaires et générer des réservations, économisant des milliers de dollars en frais de service-conseil. NAIL FIX IN THE 6IX crée des franchises dans le domaine de la beauté à l’aide de l’IA de Google Ouvrir plusieurs succursales d’un même salon de manucure entraîne de grands défis logistiques. Avec l’aide de Gemini, NAIL FIX IN THE 6IX simplifie ses flux de travail en matière de RH, de ventes et de formation, ce qui lui permet de gagner du temps, d’outiller le personnel et de créer un modèle évolutif pour favoriser la croissance de l’entreprise. Helcim propose une plateforme sécurisée et abordable, propulsée par l’IA de Google, qui aide les PME du pays (concurrence, occasions de croissance). 4Point facilite la découverte de ressources essentielles à l’aide de l’IA de Google L’exploitation minière traditionnelle nécessite temps et main-d’œuvre. 4Point utilise l’IA de Google pour identifier rapidement des cibles minérales à potentiel élevé, pour l’extraction de ressources essentielles des dizaines d’années plus vite. Topsy Farms fait grossir l’entreprise familiale avec Recherche Google Topsy Farms, une ferme familiale, vend des produits en laine sur l’île Amherst, en Ontario. En 2018, comme elle risquait de fermer ses portes, elle a dû améliorer sa visibilité. Pouvant désormais procéder plus rapidement et être concurrentiel à plus grande échelle, Baharona a transformé son projet passionnant en une entreprise prospère. Après une croissance réussie en Amérique du Nord, elle s’est tournée vers le ciblage géographique de Google Ads pour déterminer les marchés adéquats d’une expansion en fonction des affinités de produit, de la rentabilité et de la concurrence. Cependant, pour que l’entreprise prenne de l’expansion, elle avait besoin de trouver de nouveaux clients. Elle s’est donc servi des outils d’annonces propulsés par l’IA de Google pour atteindre une nouvelle clientèle de manière rentable et a pu ainsi augmenter les demandes de son traiteur, Taco Bar, de 20 %. Grâce à l’IA de Google, l’entreprise Create Makerspace constate un gain d’efficacité qui lui permet de consacrer plus de temps à sa communauté Create Makerspace est un carrefour d’innovation établi à Squamish, en Colombie-Britannique, qui souhaitait trouver un partenaire pour propulser sa productivité et ainsi consacrer plus de temps au soutien de sa communauté locale. L’équipe a choisi les produits de Google pour soutenir l’ensemble de ses activités et exploite désormais Gemini et Workspace pour simplifier les tâches laborieuses, comme la préparation de demandes de subventions, pour consacrer plus de temps à la communauté créative de sa ville. Grâce aux outils publicitaires propulsés par l’IA de Google, les affaires sont florissantes pour Karen’s Flower Shop Pour les entreprises familiales, il peut s’avérer difficile d’atteindre de nouveaux membres de la communauté avec un budget fixe. column5: Google di Malaysia - About Google around the world Jump to Content GOOGLE DI MALAYSIA Mantap Malaysia Bersama AI Sejak lebih 15 tahun lalu, Google berbangga menjadi sebahagian daripada Malaysia. Hari ini, Malaysia pantas melonjak sebagai ekonomi digital paling pesat berkembang di Asia Tenggara, dengan Nilai Barangan Kasar (GMV) mencecah AS$39 bilion . Seiring dengan potensi besar ini, kami komited untuk terus melabur di sini. Kami mahu terus bekerjasama membina sebuah negara pacuan AI yang teguh, inklusif, dan bersedia untuk masa depan. Tonton video Melindungi keselamatan rakyat Malaysia Ekonomi digital hanya boleh berkembang jika wujudnya rasa percaya. Jika orang ramai berasa tidak selamat, sudah pasti mereka teragak-agak untuk beralih ke dunia digital. Oleh itu, kami merangka perlindungan yang disesuaikan khas untuk keperluan tempatan bagi melindungi rakyat Malaysia. Memerangi penipuan melalui teknologi Ciri perlindungan penipuan yang dipertingkatkan di dalam Google Play Protect akan menyekat pemasangan aplikasi ' sideloaded ' yang berisiko secara automatik untuk melindungi pengguna Android di Malaysia. Sistem pengesahan perkhidmatan kewangan (FSV) kami pula memastikan hanya pengiklan kewangan yang sah dan berlesen sahaja dibenarkan mencapai pengguna di Malaysia melalui Google Ads. Melindungi kanak-kanak dan remaja Kami mewujudkan persekitaran digital yang selamat dari mula dengan mengaktifkan penapis SafeSearch secara automatik untuk pengguna di bawah umur 18 tahun. Pada masa sama, YouTube Kids dan ' supervised experiences ' di YouTube menawarkan kandungan tontonan yang bersesuaian dengan tahap kematangan kanak-kanak. Melalui aplikasi Family Link, kami memudahkan ibu bapa memantau aktiviti digital anak-anak. Ibu bapa boleh menetapkan had masa penggunaan aplikasi, mahupun mengehadkan tontonan YouTube Shorts kepada sifar minit , bagi memastikan anak-anak melayari internet dengan selamat dan menikmati kandungan yang sesuai dengan umur mereka. Memperjuangkan literasi digital Berbekalkan sokongan dana AS$5 juta daripada Google.org, ASEAN Foundation kini sedang memperluas program Scam Ready ASEAN di Malaysia. Menerusi kolaborasi bersama agensi impak perubahan sosial, Ratio:Cause, program ini akan melengkapkan seramai 200,000 rakyat Malaysia dalam tempoh dua tahun akan datang dengan pelbagai sumber pencegahan penipuan dalam talian agar mereka dapat melayari dunia digital dengan selamat. Tonton video Link to Youtube Video (visible only when JS is disabled) Ketahui bagaimana setiap produk Google direka dengan mengutamakan aspek keselamatan. Kami sentiasa melindungi privasi dan keselamatan anda di dalam produk-produk yang anda gemari. Lebih lanjut Memacu inovasi AI untuk sains dan masyarakat Usaha untuk membawa manfaat teknologi AI secara menyeluruh kepada rakyat Malaysia memerlukan sokongan infrastruktur tempatan yang teguh. Oleh itu, kami sedang membina Pusat Data Google dan Google Cloud Region dengan komitmen utuh terhadap kelestarian serta kecekapan tenaga perintis dalam industri—bagi memastikan kemajuan digital ini berkembang secara bertanggungjawab seiring dengan kesejahteraan komuniti. AS$2 bilion pelaburan di Malaysia bagi pembangunan Pusat Data Google dan Google Cloud Region AS$3.2 bilion anggaran sumbangan kepada KDNK negara menjelang 2030 26,500 peluang pekerjaan yang bakal disokong menjelang 2030 Kajian berbulan kini siap dalam beberapa minit Melioidosis, iaitu penyakit bawaan bakteria Burkholderia pseudomallei , meragut hampir 90,000 nyawa setiap tahun. Pasukan penyelidik dari Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) yang dianggotai oleh Dr. Su Datt Lam dan Dr. Sylvia Chieng kini memanfaatkan keupayaan AlphaFold untuk merungkai struktur protein bakteria tersebut. Usaha ini mempercepatkan potensi pasukan mereka dalam membangunkan rawatan bersasar yang mampu menyelamatkan nyawa. Tonton video Membantu warga emas dengan rehabilitasi AI Jia Ying, Loo Ying, dan Yong Kong dari inisiatif AI Ready ASEAN Challenge telah membangunkan sebuah sistem pemulihan otot pintar. Dikuasakan oleh Google AI, sistem ini mampu melaraskan terapi pemulihan secara masa nyata, membolehkan warga emas meneruskan sesi pemulihan berkualiti tinggi dengan selamat di rumah. Memacu pertumbuhan ekonomi dengan AI Rakyat Malaysia kini menunjukkan minat yang sangat mendalam terhadap teknologi AI, dengan 74% daripadanya berinteraksi menggunakan alatan AI setiap hari . Bagi merebut unjuran lonjakan ekonomi sebanyak RM130 bilion hasil daripada produktiviti berteraskan AI, kami mengambil langkah proaktif untuk memperkasakan barisan tenaga kerja yang berkhidmat untuk negara ini. 445,000 penjawat awam bakal menerima manfaat Gemini di Google Workspace memlalui inisiatif " AI at Work 2.0 " dengan kerjasama Kementerian Digital Jalinan kerjasama dengan Kerajaan Negeri Selangor bagi membina dan melaksanakan penyelesaian AI tahap tinggi demi kesejahteraan awam Akses Gemini for Education diperluaskan ke semua universiti awam di Malaysia, yang bakal memanfaatkan hampir 600,000 orang pelajar dan 75,000 orang ahli fakulti Tonton video Link to Youtube Video (visible only when JS is disabled) Gamuda telah membangunkan Botunity, sebuah platform bot sembang (chatbot) dalaman berpusat menggunakan Google Vertex AI dan Gemini Pro. column5: About Google in Malaysia - About Google around the world Jump to Content GOOGLE IN MALAYSIA Advancing Malaysia Together with AI For over 15 years, Google has proudly called Malaysia home. Today, as Malaysia emerges as Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing digital economy—reaching US$39 Billion in GMV —we are partnering to build a future-ready, AI-driven nation that is robust, inclusive, and fundamentally secure. Watch the video Keeping Malaysians Safe Online Growth in the digital economy must be anchored in a foundation of trust. If people don’t feel safe, they won’t participate. We are localising our approach to proactively protect Malaysians. Fighting financial fraud with technology The Enhanced fraud protection feature within Google Play Protect automatically blocks the installation of potentially-risky sideloaded apps to better safeguard Android users in Malaysia. New financial services verification (FSV) ensure only legitimate, licensed financial advertisers can reach users in Malaysia through Google Ads ecosystem. Protecting children and teens We create safe default environments by automatically applying our SafeSearch filter for users under 18, while YouTube Kids and supervised experiences on YouTube provide age-appropriate viewing environments based on a child's maturity level. Furthermore, we empower parents with Family Link to actively manage digital routines—from customising app time limits to setting YouTube Shorts scrolling limits to zero minutes —ensuring a secure, age-appropriate online experience. Championing digital literacy Supported with US$5 million funding from Google.org, the ASEAN Foundation is scaling Scam Ready ASEAN in Malaysia. In collaboration with social change impact agency, Ratio:Cause, the programme will reach over 200,000 Malaysians over the next two years with online scam prevention resources to navigate the digital world safely. Powered by Google AI, it adjusts therapy in real time, enabling seniors to safely continue high-quality rehabilitation at home. column5: Meer informatie over Google Nederland - About Google around the world Jump to Content GOOGLE IN NEDERLAND Het AI-potentieel van Nederland helpen ontsluiten Nederland is altijd een digitale koploper geweest, met een sterke infrastructuur, innovatieve cultuur en robuuste tech-strategie. AI heeft het potentieel om de Nederlandse economie met € 85 miljard te laten groeien, maar we moeten nu actie ondernemen en samenwerken om het potentieel volledig te ontsluiten. Lees meer De impact van Google in Nederland €4 miljard Investeringen in Nederland, waaronder in onze datacenters. 700 Werknemers in Amsterdam, Eemshaven, Middenmeer en binnenkort Winschoten. 500.000 Nederlanders digitale vaardigheden bijgebracht via trainingen. Google Nederland in vogelvlucht Voet aan wal In juni 2003 openden we voor het eerst onze deuren in Amsterdam om klanten in de Benelux te helpen met online marketing. 2​0​倍，​目前​更​匯集​了​超過 30 個​國家​與​地區​的​同仁，​一起​為​全球​科技​創新​努力、​幫助​台灣​邁向​成為​亞洲​矽谷​的​目標。 200​7 年​: YouTube 正式​在​台灣​上線 YouTube 在​台灣​邁入​第 1​7 年，​我們​見證​了​它​從​一​個​影音​平台，​蛻變成​一​個​充滿​信任​與​活力​的​生態​系；​在​這​裡，​觀眾、​創作者​和​品牌​之間，​透過​真實​的​互動​與​交流，​建立​起​深厚​的​連結。 瞭解​更多 201​3 年​: 啟用 Google 資料​中心​與 Google Cloud 雲端​區域 201​7 年​至 2​02​2 年，​Google 資料​中心​成功​在​台灣​推動​地方​經濟​發展、​振興​社區​並​強化​環境​管理​成效，​為​當地​社區​帶來​以下​方面​的​改變​；​在​這​五​年間，​Google 資料​中心​透過​直接、​間接​與​誘發​的​效益，​每​年​為​台灣​國內​生產​總值 (GDP) 貢​獻​約 49 億​美元。 我們​也​作為​最早​提供​在​地業​者​大型​基礎​建設​的​公有​雲供​應商，​透過​穩定​與​安全​的​雲端​區域 (Cloud Region) 、​各​種​雲端​科技​與​解決​方案，​洞察​當地​企業​需求，​協助​台灣​企業​面對​數​位​轉型​挑戰，​強化​營運​體質、​提升​市場​競爭力。 瞭解​更多 201​8 年​: 啟動​「Google 智慧​台灣​計畫」 這​是 Google 在​台灣​發展​以來​規模​最​大、​面向​最廣​的​外部​計畫。​透過​這​個​計畫，​我們​希望​能​從​社會​經濟​層面，​在​台灣​落實 Google AI 優先​的​願景。 多​年​來，​我們​持續​和​政府​及​產學​夥伴​合作，​一起​加速​台灣​發展、​邁向​亞洲​矽谷​的​願景。​我們​培養​科技​人才​的 A​I 創新​研究營、​支援​新創企業​的​孵創​計畫，​推出​台灣​新聞數​位​共榮​基金​推動​新聞​產業​數​位​轉型，​還​透過 Google 旗下​的​非營利組織 Google.org 挹​注​資金，​與​財團​法​人​均​一​平台教育​基金會​合作​推動​弭平學習​資源​落差、​台灣​事​實查核​中心​推廣​數​位​素養。 瞭解​更多 201​8 年​: HTC 優秀​成員​加入 Google 硬體​部​門 這​項​合作​將​使得​我們​未來​的​產品​創新​獲得​更多​助力。​這些​新夥伴​的​加入​將​會​為​Google 注入​數​十​年​專注於​智慧型​手機​產業​領域​的​經驗，​以及 HTC 具​突破性​的​技術​創新。​從 2018 起，​我們​和​新成員​將​全心​投入，​忠於​我們​的​團隊​核心​理念：​透過​Google 最佳​的 A​I 技術​與​軟硬​整合，​創造出​大幅​改善​使用​者​生活​的​體驗。 202​1 年​: 啟用 Tpark (台北​遠東​通訊園區) 全​新辦公園區 Google 美國​總部​以​外​最​大​的​硬體​研發​基地。​我們​在​台灣​的​工程​研發團​隊​集結​了​十分​多元​的​人才​領域，​包括​軟體、​硬體、​半導體​設計、​產品​開發、​品管​測試​等。​隨著​在​台灣​研發團隊​的​成長，​我們​參與​開發​的​裝置​和​技術​也​逐漸​增加，​除了 Pixel 智慧型​手機​系列，​Pixel Watch 智慧​手錶、​Fitbit 健康​穿戴​裝置、​Nest 智慧​音箱、​Chromecast 串流​媒體​播放器​等​全球​硬體​產品，​都​有​台灣​團隊​開發​與​貢獻​的​身影。​20​2​4 年，​我們​啟用​了​第二​棟​硬體​研發辦​公大樓，​持續​為​台灣​在​技術​研發​與​創新​領域​帶來​更多​成長​機會。 瞭解​更多 202​0 年​: 啟動​「數​位​人才​探索​計畫」 「數​位​人才​探索​計畫」​自 202​0 年​啟動來，​有​超過​六萬​學員​報名。​數位​技術​的​快速​發展，​為​人才​市場​帶來​前所​未見​的​挑戰​和​機會​；Google 透過​多​項​數​位​人才​培育​計畫，​提升​在​職​人士​的​數位​競爭力，​媒合、​解決​產業界​的​人才​需求。​我們​希望​能​持續​盡​一份​心力​培育​數​位​人才，​為​台灣​人才​轉型​注入​能量，​也​提升​台灣​的​產業​競爭力。 瞭解​更多 202​0 年​: 培育​在​地人​才​打擊​不實​資訊 202​0 年，​我們​開始​和​台灣​事​實查核​中心、​社團法人​社區​大學​全國​促進會、​My​GoPen，​還​有​假​新聞清潔​劑​合作，​透過​社區​大學​的​課程、​種子​志工​的​培訓​計畫，​以及​在​台灣​各​地​的​講座，​4 年​下來​累積​培訓​了​超過 1,20​0 名​的​教育​工作​者，​觸及​超過 26 萬​人次。​其中​事​實查核​中心​和​社區​大學​發展出​台灣​獨有​的​「媒體​素養​融​入式​教學」，​首先​訓練​各​種​不同​課目​的​講師​都​熟​悉事​實​查核​的​工具，​並且​在 2​00 門​不同​的​課堂​裡​融入​事​實​查核​的​環節，​讓​學員​在​不同​的​情境​自然​認識​事​實​查核​的​工具​和​重要性，​觸​及​了​超過 12,00​0 人​次​以上​的​學員。 瞭解​更多 202​4 年​: Apricot 海底​電纜​即將​啟用 你​知道 98​% 的​國際​網路​流量​都​是​經由​海底​電纜​傳輸​到​世界​各​地嗎？​隨著​人們​工作、​娛樂​和​交流​的​形式​日益​數​位化，​穩定​的​網路​連線​變得​比​以​往​更​加​重要。​Google 在​過去​幾​年間，​逐步​投資​興建於​台灣​上岸​的​國際​海底​電纜，​包括​已​啟用​的 FASTER 台灣​延伸段、 PL​CN，​及​興建​中​的 Apricot ；其中 Apricot 海底​電纜​將​連接​日本、​關島、​菲律賓、​台灣、​新加坡、​以及​印尼，​預計​在 2​02​4 年​啟用。​根據​研調​機構 Analysys Mason 的​預估，​從 202​2 年​到 2​02​6 年，​Google 投資​的​網路​基礎​建設​將​使​台灣​的​頻寬​增加 32%。 瞭解​更多 完整​報告 1 / 在​地​文化 我們​致力於​將​當地​文化​價值​融入​我們​的​產品、​服務​和​營運​之​中，​讓​世界​看見​台灣​的​獨特​魅力。 找到​自己​的​驕傲 一起​支持​台灣 L​GBTQ​+ 社群 長期​以來，​我們​以​實際​行動​支持 LGBTQ+ 族群​和​多​元​平​等​包容​理念，​除了​透過​自發性​內部​員工​社​團定​期​舉辦​專業​講座​和​活動，​強化​同仁​的​性別​平權​意識、​提倡​對於​不同​族群、​文化​的​認識​與​包容，​我們​也​持續​打造​更​具​包容性​的​產品​與​服務，​為​多元​性別​認同​的​族群​帶來​更​友善​的​使用​體驗。 台灣​珍珠​奶茶登 Google 首頁 發源於​台灣​的​珍珠​奶茶，​這​款​冰涼​飲品​通常​由​茶、​牛奶​和​珍珠粉圓​組成。​珍珠​奶茶​在​全球​廣受​歡迎，​甚至​在 2​02​0 年​被​正式​宣布​成為​新​的​表情​符號。 幫助​台灣​音樂​人​邁向​國際​舞台 臺灣​擁有​多元​的​音樂​人才​與​創作​資源，​使​其​流行​音樂​在​華語樂壇​中佔​有​重要​地位。​YouTube 希望​幫助​音樂人​深入​了​解頻道​觀眾​組成、​喜好​等​內容​數據​分析​與​經營​策略，​紮根​各​國​市場、​走向​海外。 發揮​台灣 A​I 潛能 Google 正​透過​在​地夥伴​關係，​掌握 AI 契機，​並​以​我們​的 A​I 驅動​的​產品​和​數​位​服務​支援​全民​與​企業。 新台幣 1.9 兆 A​I 可​使​台灣​經濟​價值​提升​逾​新台幣 1.9 兆（​約 และเสริมสร้างความปลอดภัยในโลกออนไลน์ ดูข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม สร้างทักษะใหม่และการเติบโตในสายอาชีพให้คนไทยผ่านโครงการ Samart Skills AI เพื่อการวิเคราะห์โรคเบาหวานขึ้น จอประสาทตา สามารถช่วยบุคลากร ทางการแพทย์ ในการคัดกรองและช่วย ให้ผู้ป่วยขอรับความช่วยเหลือได้ ตั้งแต่ระยะเริ่มต้น เสริมสร้างทักษะดิจิทัลให้คนไทยรู้เท่าทันกลลวงออนไลน์ สร้างความก้าวหน้าด้าน AI ด้วยเทคโนโลยีของ Google ดูวีดีโอ Link to Youtube Video (visible only when JS is disabled) ผลิตภัณฑ์ที่มีประโยชน์สำหรับทุกคน ที่ Google เราพัฒนาผลิตภัณฑ์ที่เป็นประโยชน์สำหรับทุกคน ช่วยให้คุณค้นหาข้อมูล เชื่อมต่อกับผู้อื่น และใช้ชีวิตได้อย่างมีประสิทธิภาพยิ่งขึ้น เปลี่ยนรูปแบบการทำงานร่วมกันของผู้คนด้วย Google Workspace ให้ทุกวันของคุณปลอดภัยยิ่งขึ้นด้วย Google กับผลิตภัณฑ์ที่มีความปลอดภัยโดยค่าเริ่มต้นและออกแบบมาเพื่อความเป็นส่วนตัว มุ่งมั่นที่จะพัฒนาคุณภาพชีวิตของผู้คน Google มุ่งมั่นสร้างสรรค์เทคโนโลยีและโครงการที่ช่วยยกระดับชีวิตคนไทย นำไปสู่สังคมที่เติบโตอย่างยั่งยืน เรียนรู้เพิ่มเติม ช่วยให้เด็กๆ เข้าถึงทักษะที่จำเป็นต่อการเป็นพลเมืองยุคดิจิทัลได้อย่างปลอดภัยด้วย Be Internet Awesome Gemini Academy ช่วยเปิดโอกาสให้ครูได้เรียนรู้เกี่ยวกับ AI แบบผสานรวมที่จะช่วยยกระดับเส้นทางการเรียนรู้ไปพร้อมกับเพิ่มประสิทธิภาพการทำงานของครู ผลลัพธ์เชิงบวกจาก Google ในประเทศไทย > 1.50 แสนล้านบาท คือผลประโยชน์ทางเศรษฐกิจที่เกิดขึ้นในปี 2022 จากการใช้ผลิตภัณฑ์และโซลูชันที่ทำงานด้วยระบบ AI ของ Google ดูข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม > 250,000 ตําแหน่งงาน จากการส่งเสริมการสร้างงานในระบบเศรษฐกิจดิจิทัล ดูข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม 4.58 แสนล้านบาท คือผลประโยชน์ทางเศรษฐกิจที่ครัวเรือนในประเทศไทยได้รับจากการใช้ผลิตภัณฑ์และโซลูชันของ Google ในปี 2022 ซึ่งคิดเป็นมูลค่าเท่ากับ 7,390 บาทต่อปี สำหรับผู้ใช้อินเทอร์เน็ตหนึ่งราย ดูข้อมูลเพิ่มเติม รายงานผลลัพธ์ทางเศรษฐกิจปี 2023 จาก Google รายงานผลลัพธ์ทางเศรษฐกิจ: ส่งเสริมการเข้าถึง AI ในประเทศไทยอย่างเท่าเทียมด้วย Google เรียนรู้เพิ่มเติม รับข่าวสารล่าสุดจาก Google ทางอีเมล ลงทะเบียนเพื่อรับข้อมูลประจำสัปดาห์จากทั่วโลก ตั้งแต่การเปิดตัวผลิตภัณฑ์ไปจนถึงเคล็ดลับในชีวิตประจำวัน สมัครรับข่าวสาร

column5: A new era of American innovation - About Google around the world Jump to Content Google is helping America become stronger, safer and more competitive than ever before. Helping Americans prosper Supporting government innovation Strengthening the American economy Play animation Pause animation Google is investing in America 26 states with a Google office or data center. Google employed more than 100,000 people full-time throughout the U.S. at the end of 2025. 19.5M+ American businesses used Google’s tools at no cost to receive phone calls, bookings, reviews, requests for directions, or other direct connections to their customers in 2025. 13M+ Americans since 2017 have been trained in digital skills through our Grow with Google network of more than 9,000 partner organizations – including local libraries, schools, and nonprofits. $1B Over the next three years, Google is providing over $1 billion to support AI education, job training programs, and other education-related initiatives in the U.S. Google Economic Impact Report Learn about our impact, state by state. Released in 2026. Learn more Helping Americans prosper At Google, we're committed to helping all Americans access the benefits of AI. For well over a decade, we’ve been integrating AI into our products and advancing the field of scientific research to make daily life easier and power breakthroughs that are expanding the realm of what’s possible. Google Gemini helps teachers create lessons that inspire all kinds of learners Helping you avoid scams with Circle to Search Partnership and the power of AI are fueling a new era of American innovation 1 / Portraits of AI Across America : Meet the people using AI to grow and serve their communities To capture how folks across the country are using AI to help fuel a new era of American innovation, we’re sharing stories from all 50 states. ASCO is turning to Google AI to equip oncologists with the latest research The American Society of Clinical Oncology is building the tools for faster, easier access to trusted cancer care and treatment information with Google AI. How Google Beam & USO are connecting military families globally We’re working with the USO to launch Google Beam globally to bring AI-powered 3D video communication to deployed military and their families. The National Cancer Institute spurs scientific discoveries with Google AI, so breakthroughs happen sooner The National Cancer Institute developed NanCI, an app that uses Google AI to help cancer researchers collaborate, share data, identify patterns, and recommend research papers, ultimately accelerating the pace of scientific discovery. Detecting smaller wildfires with better frequency using a constellation of satellites Google partnered with leaders in the fire community to create FireSat - a purpose-built constellation of satellites designed to detect and track wildfires as small as a classroom. Color Health supports early cancer detection and treatment with Google AI to help improve patient outcomes Color Health’s Virtual Cancer Clinic, built with Google AI, helps accelerate and target the care process from screening through treatment and survivorship. Using AI to help communities better predict natural disasters with Groundsource Groundsource, a new Gemini-powered methodology, transforms millions of public reports into a high-quality data archive to aid crisis prediction — starting with urban flash floods. AlphaFold 3 predicts the structure and interactions of all of life’s molecules Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold is accelerating the pace of scientific innovation by helping researchers predict the intricate 3D shapes of proteins. MLB ™ is creating personalized, engaging experiences for fans and helping teams better understand the possibilities within their data MLB ™ leverages Google Cloud AI to contextualize more than 15 million data points in real time every game, delivering insights that deepen the fan experience and reveal previously unseen connections. Unlocking new ways to communicate across language barriers for more than half a billion people Google Translate breaks down language barriers to help people connect and better understand the world around them. Now, we’re using AI to expand the variety of languages we support. Load More Supporting government innovation Governments are beginning to see how AI can help them serve their communities better, faster and with limited resources. From fixing potholes to addressing threats to public health, AI can support a government’s ability to deliver on its promises. To help local governments seize AI’s potential, Google has partnered with the U.S. Conference of Mayors to develop an AI Playbook that equips leaders with foundational steps and replicable examples for responsible AI adoption. The U.S. Department of Transportation is the first cabinet-level agency to fully transition from legacy providers to Google Workspace. By equipping staff with Google AI tools to rapidly synthesize research and streamline contracting, the U.S. DOT is directly strengthening the safety and reliability of our nation’s transit systems. NOAA's National Hurricane Center, with support from Google AI, is giving people more decision-making confidence and more time to prepare. Google is working with the NHC to provide earlier, more accurate predictions to agencies, emergency services, and the public. The Air Force Research Laboratory partnered with Google Cloud to leverage AI to tackle complex challenges, from materials science and bioinformatics to human performance optimization. Covered California is simplifying the insurance process with Google AI to automate verification of documents in seconds instead of weeks, allowing staff to focus on ensuring families get the care they need without delay. The City of Los Angeles is equipping city workers with Google AI, helping to accelerate communications, automate time-sensitive tasks, and streamline complex projects, ultimately delivering faster and more accessible public services for the city's four million residents. The State of Connecticut is using Google Al to identify and respond to cybersecurity threats faster and more effectively, reducing forensic investigation times from months to hours. The City of Chattanooga, TN is using Google Al to centralize crash data, with the aim of making more informed, life-saving decisions: from prioritizing new traffic signals or redesigned crosswalks, to reallocating police patrols to high-risk corridors. The Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority is partnering with Google Cloud to develop smarter tolling systems. By applying Al, CTRMA is providing efficiency across the tolling experience, from pricing to processing, resulting in reduced congestion and better traffic flow for Texans. The Oklahoma Department of Transportation partnered with Google Cloud to use AI to monitor bridge conditions and prioritize maintenance needs, helping ensure safe and efficient travel for Oklahomans. Google partnered with the Department of Veterans Affairs to enable developers to create new tools and applications that make it easier for veterans to access healthcare, submit claims, and manage their benefits. 1 / Strengthening the American economy We’re already seeing the ways AI is strengthening the American economy by helping American businesses and workers solve problems, save time, and accomplish more with their resources. At Google, we’re investing heavily in AI development and technical infrastructure, empowering businesses of all sizes with leading technology, and providing access to training and resources to ensure opportunities of AI are widely shared. Google AI helps small businesses get back to what they love Walmart is equipping associates with practical AI training from Google to help grow their careers Google is partnering with Walmart to develop customized learning programs to help Walmart employees gain new skills. Developed by Google experts, the Google AI Professional Certificate equips associates with the AI skills to improve how they work, so they can provide a better customer experience and further their careers. Preparing 300,000+ skilled trades workers for America’s future Google.org's $50M commitment helps prepare skilled trades workers for in-demand careers nationwide. Leading training organizations—electrical training ALLIANCE, International Training Institute for the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Industry, TradesFutures, and United Association's International Training Fund—will use the funding to modernize and expand access to apprenticeship programs. Bringing the best of Google Gemini and AI training to college students We launched the Google AI for Education Accelerator to offer free AI training and Google Career Certificates to college students across America. Over 400 public universities, including the University of Michigan, Ohio State University, the University of Virginia and the University Systems in Texas, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania have signed up. Google is partnering with local chambers of commerce and SBDCs to train Americans in AI skills Google is partnering with local chambers of commerce and small business development centers (SBDCs) for an in-person “Make AI Work for You” tour. These hands-on workshops will help small businesses use AI to solve key challenges, tackle delayed tasks, brainstorm solutions, and automate repetitive work with a personalized action plan. Helping small businesses reach their customers with Google AI Etsy shops are full of unique stories and special finds, but getting them in front of the right buyers can be a challenge. Using Google AI, Etsy is helping shoppers discover these creations and making it easier for sellers to connect with the people who’ll love them most. Google is offering free AI training and tools to U.S. small businesses, so they can grow their communities Built by Google experts, the Google AI Professional Certificate equips small businesses with practical AI skills. Through hands-on projects, they can start using AI to get more done and unlock new opportunities for their business. Google and Cook County are equipping communities with AI skills, so they can build career opportunities Through a collaboration between Cook County’s Project Rainbow Initiative and Grow with Google, no-cost scholarships will be made available for Google Career Certificates, helping hundreds of residents gain the skills they need to grow their careers or start new ones in fields such as cybersecurity and data analytics. Supporting small business growth with AI tools Veteran-owned GO-KOT uses Google AI-powered advertising tools to transform their online presence, connecting with new customers nationwide. They also use Google AI tools to help with marketing and customer-facing communications, saving them time to focus on their goal of growing GO-KOT and hiring more people. Safeguarding deliveries with AI UPS Capital launched DeliveryDefense Address Confidence, which uses machine learning and UPS data to provide a confidence score for shippers to help them determine the likelihood of a successful delivery. Helping farmers through weather forecasting Benchmark Labs uses Vertex AI to develop weather forecasting and insights tailored to specific locations, helping farmers gain more actionable alerts at a microclimate level across their farms. Accelerating innovation in the auto industry Ford and Google are collaborating to optimize database management, with the aim to fully harness the potential of managed services, generative AI, and cloud database technology to drive efficiency, resilience, and innovation. Boosting family-owned business revenue Hill Top Contractors, a storage tank removal, environmental remediation and construction company based in Roanoke, VA, uses Google’s AI-powered search to inform their business practices - helping them stay up-to-date on industry regulations and equipment maintenance information.
